Notes:
  search returns, by default: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as complete function bodies),
  RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus the other tests that cover the same code (ALSO COVERING —
  they all have to keep passing), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the queried concept is
  named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC — the sweep, so you need no grep), VERIFY (the narrowest test
  command for the file, derived from the repo's own build files) and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a
  switch over an enum/sealed set would throw at runtime rather than fail to compile. The three
  reference blocks — container map, signature types, declaration card — are OFF by default because
  they measurably cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all (or the individual flags,
  or ENTIRE_GRAPH_REFERENCE_BLOCKS) turns them back on for interactive reading.
  search --top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the
  exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every
  eligible file). neighbors/impact take --symbol <file>:<line>, or --symbol NAME with

  impl blocks, receiver methods, extension members, partial parts, one hop of trait/module/base
  acquisition). It reports a method's owning type, and for a trait/interface it reports who
  implements it. Membership is never inferred from a name resembling another name.
  stats is a local read-only report for humans: it reads the coding-agent session transcripts
  already on disk (~/.claude/projects/<path-slug>/*.jsonl) and reports graph usage vs
  grep/read exploration, bytes each pulled into context, and an ESTIMATED token saving whose
  assumption is printed with the number. --transcript narrows it to ONE session transcript
  (plus that session's subagent transcripts) instead of a whole project directory.
  index --report writes a human-readable GRAPH_REPORT.md beside the JSON summary: what the
  graph found in this tree (languages and their tier, symbol kinds, relations, top files,
  warnings) rendered from the snapshot itself, so the same tree always renders the same bytes.
  The committed-tree cache defaults to the platform's per-user cache directory (macOS
  ~/Library/Caches/entire-graph, XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache elsewhere); --cache-dir and
  ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR override it and --no-cache disables it. --worktree is never cached.
  --include-file contains gitignore-style rules that re-include ignored paths; it is not an allowlist.
  Streaming NDJSON writes aggregate stats and completeness in the trailing summary record.
  commit/diff/analyze stop cleanly after --max-seconds (default 120; 0 = unlimited) and emit the
  partial result with W_ANALYSIS_BUDGET_EXCEEDED warnings listing what was skipped.

=== README ===
# Entire Graph

**This release is for your agents.**

Entire Graph gives coding agents a precomputed, deterministic map of your codebase — every
function, type, route, and call relationship — so they can start from ranked
structural evidence instead of broad grep-and-read exploration. It is 100% local:
no network, no model calls, no keys.

## Install (one minute)

Go 1.24+ and a C compiler required first

```sh
go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-graph@main
entire plugin install "$(go env GOBIN | grep . || echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin")/entire-graph" --force
```

Then, in any repo your agents work in:

```sh
entire graph init-agents
```

That's it. `init-agents` drops the operating guide into your project's `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`,
so Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Pi — any agent that reads those files — picks up the
search-first workflow automatically. No config, no MCP server, no daemon.

## Status line: estimated exploration savings

A one-line Claude Code badge, updated as the session runs:

```text
[GRAPH] ↗ 2.1M saved · 28 search · 9 impact · graph-first ✓ · 75% of locates · 12% of session
```

- **saved** — heuristic estimated tokens, not a measured counterfactual or
  evidence of end-to-end task savings; it uses the same model as
  `entire graph stats`.
- **verb split** — top three graph verbs by call count for this session.
- **graph-first** — did the session open with a graph call rather than grep/read.
- **of locates** — share of all locate-ish calls (graph vs `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob`/shell `grep|find|cat`)
  that went to the graph.
- **of session** — the estimate as a share of billed session tokens.

Before any graph call it reads `[GRAPH] no graph calls yet · 35 explore`, and if the binary or
transcript is missing it prints nothing at all.

Enable it in `~/.claude/settings.json` (or `.claude/settings.json` for one project):

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "sh /path/to/entire-graph/scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh"
  }
}
```

Installed as a plugin, the path is `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh"`.
The plugin manifest declares the same block under `settings`, but Claude Code only merges an
allowlisted subset of plugin-provided settings (`agent`, `subagentStatusLine` as of 2.1.219) and
drops `statusLine` — so today the settings.json entry above is what actually turns it on. The
manifest entry costs nothing and starts working if that allowlist widens.

Knobs: `ENTIRE_GRAPH_BIN` (explicit binary path), `NO_COLOR`,
`ENTIRE_GRAPH_STATUSLINE_CACHE=0` (disable the render cache),
`ENTIRE_GRAPH_STATUSLINE_SCOPE=project` (whole-project totals instead of this session — it
re-scans the entire transcript directory, which is far slower; the default `session` scope reads
one transcript).

## What your agents get

| agent workflow | before | with Entire Graph |
|---|---|---|
| **Locate a fix** | repeated grep/open cycles | `entire graph search` → inspect focused source → edit and verify |
| **Impact of a change** | repo-wide grep for callers | `entire graph impact --symbol X` — callers, type consumers, data flow, co-change in one shot |
| **Review a diff** | file-by-file reading | `entire graph diff` — entity-level changes with dependent counts |

The search understands natural language ("XTRIM trims wrong stream entries"), ranks real
implementation code above tests and docs, bridges vocabulary gaps through the call graph, and
returns budgeted output designed to drop straight into an agent's context.

Want the exact agent instructions? `entire graph agent-guide` prints them; they
also live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). The current guide is resolution-first: use
the graph to locate and understand the change, then verify the result.

## Where it fits in Entire

Entire Graph is the **semantic layer** of the Entire platform — infrastructure, not another
workflow to learn:

- **Entire Search / Why / Blame** consume it to answer developer questions with entity-level
  precision.
- **Checkpoints and Trails** use its `diff`/`commit` analysis to describe what an agent actually
  changed.

You (a human) will mostly experience it *through* those surfaces. Your agents call it directly.

## Evidence status

The former 54.9% Haiku, 57.7% Sonnet, and 31–73% open-model token-savings
figures are withdrawn. They were token-first measurements under a prompt policy
that encouraged the graph arms to stop early and did not require equivalent
resolution evidence from every arm. “Patch produced” was also reported as task
completion, which is not the same as passing the task's tests.

A replacement claim requires:

- identical tool-agnostic working instructions across arms;
- each tool's normal interface;
- official task resolution as the primary outcome;
- token and turn comparisons over commonly resolved tasks;
- repeated runs with uncertainty; and
- pinned binaries, prompts, datasets, and retained raw artifacts.

Until that evidence is frozen, `entire graph stats` and the status line are
local heuristic reports only, not benchmark results.

## More

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) — the agent operating guide (also: `entire graph agent-guide`)
- [docs/DETAILS.md](docs/DETAILS.md) — full command reference, architecture, language support,
  performance and accuracy benchmarks, security model
- `entire graph help` — command list; `entire graph doctor --json` — environment check

export const meta = {
  name: 'understand-entire-graph',
  description: 'Deep-read every subsystem of entire-graph and verify its mechanics live',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Read', detail: 'parallel deep readers over each subsystem' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'run the real binary and check the claimed mechanics' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph'

const READER_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    area: { type: 'string' },
    summary: { type: 'string', description: '5-10 sentences, dense, mechanism-level. No filler.' },
    mechanisms: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Every distinct mechanism you found, in causal order. Be exhaustive.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          name: { type: 'string' },
          how: { type: 'string', description: 'Telegraphic but COMPLETE on how it actually works: inputs, algorithm, outputs, thresholds, constants.' },
          cite: { type: 'string', description: 'file:line (repo-relative), comma-separated for multiple' },
        },
        required: ['name', 'how', 'cite'],
      },
    },
    data_shapes: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Key structs/records/on-disk formats with field names and cite' },
    knobs: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'Env vars / flags / defaults that change behavior, with default values' },
    gotchas: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    open_questions: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['area', 'summary', 'mechanisms'],
}

const PREAMBLE = `You are deep-reading the repo at ${ROOT} (Go; the 'entire-graph' code-intelligence engine shipped as the 'entire graph' CLI subcommand). Goal: an EXHAUSTIVE, mechanism-level understanding of your assigned area so a senior engineer could reimplement it.

Rules:
- Read the actual source. Do not guess from names. Open the big files and follow the control flow end to end.
- Use rtk (rtk <cmd>) for shell commands where it applies; it is a token-saving proxy.
- Cite every claim as repo-relative file:line.
- Output style: CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED. Telegraphic, no articles-where-droppable, no hedging, no restating the question, no "I found that". BUT never drop substance: keep every constant, threshold, field name, algorithm step, and ordering fact. Compress style, not content.
- If you find something surprising or that contradicts the docs, say so in gotchas.
- Do not edit any file.

YOUR AREA:
`

const AREAS = [
  {
    key: 'cli-surface',
    prompt: `CLI surface + command wiring.
Read internal/cli/*.go (root.go, search.go, def.go, neighbors.go, impact.go, index.go, stats.go, changed.go, verify.go, completeness.go, agents.go, report.go, env.go, callsite.go, symbolref.go, search_session.go, search_pathscope.go) and cmd/entire-graph/main.go.
Answer: full command inventory and what each does; how flags/env are parsed and defaulted; how a symbol selector (NAME vs file:line vs --file/--line/--kind) is resolved and what the ambiguity error looks like (internal/cli/symbolref.go); the output formats (json/ndjson/text/agent) and who renders them; how --max-context-bytes budgeting is enforced at the CLI layer; how the plugin entrypoint is invoked by the parent 'entire' CLI (entire-plugin.yml, .claude-plugin/); exit codes and error surfaces.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'parsing-engine',
    prompt: `Parsing / symbol extraction engine — the front end.
Read internal/sem/parser.go (~7.8k LOC), internal/sem/provider.go (~17.9k LOC), internal/sem/grammars/, internal/sem/inventory_languages.go, shebang.go, ignore.go, and the per-language files at a survey level (rust.go, typescript.go, java.go, php.go, ruby.go, swift.go, kotlin.go, groovy.go, haskell.go, ocaml.go, perl.go, csharp.go, dart.go, erlang.go, protobuf.go, yaml.go, shell.go, flowjs.go, gobuild.go, cpp_specialization.go, pgsql/).
Answer: what parser technology is used (tree-sitter? hand-rolled? both?) and how grammars are bound/built; how a file is routed to a language (extension, shebang, content sniff); what the LANGUAGE TIERS are (full-relations vs inventory-only) and what determines the tier; how symbols are extracted per language and normalized into one model; how nested containers / methods / impl blocks / partial classes are handled (nested_containers.go, member_join_test.go); how file discovery + ignore rules work (ignore.go, gitignore semantics, --ignore-file/--include-file, worktree vs committed tree); parse failure handling and completeness reporting; performance strategy (concurrency, memory, budgets).`,
  },
  {
    key: 'graph-model',
    prompt: `The graph data model + snapshot/analysis records.
Read internal/sem/types.go (~3.4k LOC), model.go, analyze.go, records_cache.go, and the snapshot/symbols/edges NDJSON emitters (find them — likely in internal/sem and internal/cli).
Answer: the exact node and edge taxonomy (every SymbolKind, every relation/EdgeKind) with what produces each; the on-the-wire record schemas for 'graph snapshot', 'graph symbols', 'graph edges' (field names, IDs, how a symbol is uniquely identified, stability of IDs across runs); how spans/line ranges are represented; what the trailing summary record contains (aggregate stats, completeness); how routes are detected and modeled; how 'analyze' composes an entity-level result and what warnings exist (e.g. W_ANALYSIS_BUDGET_EXCEEDED); determinism guarantees (sorting, stable ordering).`,
  },
  {
    key: 'edge-resolution',
    prompt: `Call/reference edge RESOLUTION — the hard part: turning a call site into an edge to a definition.
Read internal/sem/call_scanners.go, python_calls.go, js_scopes.go, dependents.go, cpp_specialization.go, and the resolution tests (call_resolution_precision_test.go, go_interface_calls_test.go, go_package_scope_test.go, function_binding_test.go, member_join_test.go).
Answer: the general resolution algorithm and its scoping rules; how ambiguity is handled (multiple candidates — dropped? all kept? ranked?); language-specific resolution strategies (Go package scope + interface method calls, Python, JS/TS scope chains, C++ template specialization); what is deliberately NOT resolved (dynamic dispatch, reflection, aliases) and how that shows up; how 'dependents' (reverse edges) are computed and stored; precision-vs-recall choices with evidence from the tests; membership edges (inherent impls, receiver methods, extension members, trait/interface implementations) and the rule that membership is never inferred from name similarity.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'search-ranking',
    prompt: `Search RANKING — how a natural-language query becomes a ranked list of candidate fix sites.
Read internal/sem/search.go (~4.8k LOC) focusing on the ranking pipeline, plus similarity.go, search_matcher.go, search_needle.go, search_testrank.go, search_file_class.go, search_boilerplate.go, search_near_dupe.go, search_mirror_dedup.go, search_confidence.go, search_section.go, search_topk_continuity_test.go, search_unmatched_terms_test.go.
Answer: end-to-end query pipeline (tokenization, term weighting, acronym/camelCase/snake handling, code-token vs prose handling); the SPARSE pass (BM25?) and what --deep changes; the SEMANTIC/structural pass (is there an embedding model, or is 'semantic' purely structural/lexical?); how the two are FUSED and with what weights; every scoring boost/penalty with its constant (exact-token bonus, test demotion, doc demotion, boilerplate suppression, near-dupe/mirror dedup, file-class weighting); how call-graph expansion bridges vocabulary gaps; the confidence tiering and the narrow-to-3 / widen-to-12 behavior; top-k continuity guarantees; what determines final ordering and tie-breaks.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'search-payload',
    prompt: `Search PAYLOAD composition — what the agent actually receives and how each block is built.
Read internal/sem/search_enclosure.go, search_related.go, search_covertest.go, search_literals.go, search_closedset.go, search_verify.go (~1.9k LOC), search_typecard.go, search_container_map.go, search_sigtypes.go, search_blocks.go, search_outline.go, search_span_merge.go, search_reanchor.go, search_locator_window.go, search_contract.go, and internal/cli/search.go rendering.
Answer: every output block in order (top hits as complete function bodies, RELATED SITES, COVERING TEST + ALSO COVERING, SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL with EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC tags, VERIFY, CLOSED-SET WARNING, and the three off-by-default reference blocks) — for EACH: what it is, the algorithm that produces it, and why it exists; how the enclosure/span logic picks exactly what source text to include and merges overlapping spans; how VERIFY derives the narrowest test command from the repo's own build files (which build systems are supported, tiers, and the probe/guard logic); how COVERING TEST is computed; how CLOSED-SET WARNING detects a switch over an enum/sealed set; how the byte budget (--max-context-bytes, default 24576) is allocated and what gets truncated first; why the reference blocks are off by default.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'index-cache',
    prompt: `Indexing, caching, and incrementality.
Read internal/sem/search_cache.go, records_cache.go, internal/cli/index.go, internal/filedigest/, internal/gitutil/, internal/sem/ignore.go (caching aspects), and the cache tests (search_cache_test.go, search_cache_worktree_test.go).
Answer: what 'entire graph index' actually builds and where it is stored (paths per platform: macOS ~/Library/Caches/entire-graph, XDG); the CACHE KEY — exactly what goes into it (tree hash? file digests? profile? binary version?) and what does NOT (this matters: a known trap is the cache being tree-keyed rather than binary-keyed, so two different builds share a cache); the --profile levels (syntax-only | fast | full) and what work each does/skips; --head vs worktree and why worktree is never cached; incremental reuse — is it per-file or whole-tree; --max-indexed-files / --index-all-files limits; cold vs warm cost; invalidation and staleness behavior; --no-cache / --cache-dir / ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'def-neighbors-impact',
    prompt: `The structural query commands: def, neighbors, impact, and the changed/diff-adjacent helpers.
Read internal/cli/def.go, internal/cli/neighbors.go, internal/cli/impact.go, internal/cli/changed.go, internal/cli/callsite.go, internal/sem/dependents.go, internal/sem/search_typecard.go (as used by def).
Answer: for EACH command — inputs, algorithm, output shape, budget, and defaults. Specifically: how 'def' assembles a declaration card (fields, associated functions/methods, one hop of trait/module/base acquisition, who-implements-this for a trait/interface); how 'neighbors' traverses (--relation, --direction in/out/both, --depth 1|2, --limit, --internal-only, --exclude-tests) and how it bounds output; how 'impact' composes its one-shot answer (callers, callees, type consumers, DATA FLOW, CO-CHANGE, SIBLINGS) — especially where co-change data comes from (git history?) and how data flow is computed; how test exclusion works; what 'changed' does.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'checkpoint-integration',
    prompt: `Entire-platform integration: commit / checkpoint / diff / analyze, plus doctor, capabilities, version, and the plugin contract.
Read internal/sem/analyze.go, internal/gitutil/, the cli handlers for commit/checkpoint/diff/analyze/doctor/capabilities/version (find them in internal/cli or cmd/), entire-plugin.yml, .claude-plugin/, and docs/BRAIN-VS-GRAPH.md.
Answer: what 'graph commit [rev]' and 'graph checkpoint <id>' compute and who consumes the output (Entire checkpoints/trails); how 'graph diff --base --head' produces entity-level change records and dependent counts; the --max-seconds budget mechanism and how partial results + W_ANALYSIS_BUDGET_EXCEEDED are emitted; what 'capabilities --json' reports and how a caller should feature-detect; what 'doctor' checks; how this binary is registered and invoked as an 'entire' plugin (the plugin manifest contract, how the parent CLI dispatches 'entire graph ...' into this binary); the relationship and division of labour between entire-graph and entire-brain per BRAIN-VS-GRAPH.md.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'agent-integration',
    prompt: `Agent-facing integration: the operating guide, stats, status line, skills, and hooks.
Read AGENTS.md (repo root, 15KB), internal/cli/stats.go (~1.2k LOC), internal/cli/agents.go, scripts/ (especially entire-graph-statusline.sh), skills/, .claude-plugin/, .claude/, .codex/, .entire/.
Answer: what 'agent-guide' prints and what 'init-agents' installs, where, and how it avoids clobbering existing AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md; how 'stats' works — which transcripts it reads (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl), how it classifies a tool call as graph vs locate-ish (Read/Grep/Glob/shell grep|find|cat), how bytes are counted, and the EXACT token-savings estimation formula and its stated assumption; how the status line renders (fields, caching, scope=session|project, ENTIRE_GRAPH_STATUSLINE_* knobs, NO_COLOR, the missing-binary path); what skills/ ships; any hooks. Quote the savings formula precisely and note explicitly that it is a heuristic, not a measured counterfactual.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'docs-design',
    prompt: `Design intent, evidence status, and roadmap — from the repo's own documentation.
Read docs/DETAILS.md, docs/adr/*, docs/language-support.md, docs/benchmarks.md, docs/baseline-report.md, docs/semantic_provider_requirements.md, docs/v2-plan.md, docs/operations.md, docs/progress-so-far.md, docs/validation/*, README.md, CLAUDE.md, ISSUE.md, FOUR-ARM-FAIRNESS-ISSUES.md.
Answer: the stated architecture and design principles (deterministic, local-only, no model calls — verify the docs actually claim this and whether anything contradicts it); the full language-support matrix with tiers; the security/privacy model; what performance numbers the docs claim and under what method; the EVIDENCE STATUS — which token-savings claims are live vs WITHDRAWN and exactly why they were withdrawn (README says 54.9%/57.7%/31-73% are withdrawn — get the full reasoning and the criteria for a replacement claim); every ADR with its decision; the v2 plan's direction. Be precise about what is measured vs asserted. Ignore the OPUS-35-PLAN-*.md files (benchmark campaign scratch, out of scope) except to note in one line what they are.`,
  },
]

phase('Read')
const notes = await parallel(AREAS.map(a => () =>
  agent(PREAMBLE + a.prompt, { label: `read:${a.key}`, phase: 'Read', schema: READER_SCHEMA })
))

phase('Verify')
const VERIFY_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    checks: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          command: { type: 'string', description: 'exact command run' },
          observed: { type: 'string', description: 'what actually happened, with numbers' },
          verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['CONFIRMED', 'REFUTED', 'PARTIAL', 'COULD_NOT_TEST'] },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'command', 'observed', 'verdict'],
      },
    },
    surprises: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['checks'],
}

const VPRE = `You are LIVE-VERIFYING the entire-graph CLI. Binary: the 'entire graph ...' subcommand (parent CLI at /Users/suhaan/.local/bin/entire); a standalone build also exists at ${ROOT}/entire-graph. Rules:
- ACTUALLY RUN the commands. A claim without a command behind it is a hypothesis, not a check.
- Use a scratch cache dir under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/b0108f24-43a4-413e-94c9-bd361b6fafc5/scratchpad so you do not disturb the user's real cache; note when you do.
- Never modify the user's repos. Read-only commands only. Do not run 'init-agents' anywhere except a throwaway temp dir you create.

- Output CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED but keep every number.

YOUR CHECKS:

const VERIFIERS = [
  {
    key: 'search-behavior',
    prompt: `Verify the SEARCH surface empirically.
1. Run 'entire graph search --repo ${ROOT} --profile full --query "how does the search rank test files below implementation"' with --format agent and separately --format json. Capture the FULL block structure of the output (names of every section that appears, in order) and the total byte size.
2. Cold vs warm: time the same search with a fresh --cache-dir vs a second run against the same cache dir. Report both wall times and the cache dir size on disk.
3. Compare --profile syntax-only vs fast vs full on the same query: wall time, number of hits, which blocks appear.
4. Run with and without --deep on the same query: wall time, whether the top hit changes, hit-set overlap.
5. Run with --reference-blocks all and diff which blocks appear vs default; report added bytes.
6. Vary --max-context-bytes (e.g. 4096 vs 24576 vs 65536) and report what gets truncated first.
7. Run a search on a TypeScript repo (/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire.io) and report whether the block set differs from Go (especially VERIFY and COVERING TEST).
Report each as a check with the exact command and observed numbers.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'structure-commands',
    prompt: `Verify the STRUCTURAL surface empirically.
1. 'entire graph capabilities --json' — dump it. Which languages, which tiers, which relations are reported? Does it match docs/language-support.md?
2. 'entire graph symbols --repo ${ROOT} --format ndjson' and 'entire graph edges ...' — capture the exact JSON field names of one record of each kind, plus the trailing summary record verbatim. Count records and report the aggregate stats.
3. 'entire graph snapshot' — same: record schema + summary.
4. Determinism: run 'symbols' twice and diff the output byte-for-byte. Same for 'edges'. Report whether ordering is stable.
5. 'entire graph def' on a real type in the repo (pick a substantial struct in internal/sem/types.go) and on an interface — does it list fields, methods, and implementors as documented?
6. 'entire graph neighbors --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in' and '--direction out' on a real function; then --depth 2 and --limit variations. Report output shape and counts.
7. 'entire graph impact --symbol X' on the same function — which sections come back (callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)? Is co-change populated, and does it look like it came from git history?
8. Trigger the AMBIGUITY error: find a name defined more than once and call neighbors on the bare name. Paste the error verbatim.
9. 'entire graph doctor --json' and 'entire graph version --json'.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'local-and-diff',
    prompt: `Verify the LOCAL-ONLY claim, the diff/analyze surface, and stats.
1. LOCAL-ONLY: prove the binary makes no network calls during a search. Use whatever is available on macOS without sudo — e.g. run the search and concurrently sample 'lsof -p <pid> -i' in a loop, or check with 'nettop'/'lsof' snapshots; also grep the source tree for outbound HTTP clients (net/http Client usage, api keys, model endpoints) under ${ROOT}/internal and ${ROOT}/cmd and report what you find. 2. 'entire graph diff --base HEAD~5 --head HEAD --repo ${ROOT} --json' — dump the record shape; are dependent counts present? Try 'analyze' and 'commit' too.
3. Budget: run diff/analyze with '--max-seconds 1' and confirm a partial result with W_ANALYSIS_BUDGET_EXCEEDED appears; paste it.
4. 'entire graph index --repo ${ROOT} --report <scratch>/GRAPH_REPORT.md --cache-dir <scratch>' — report what the JSON summary contains and the headings of the generated report. Run twice and confirm the report bytes are identical.
5. 'entire graph stats --repo /Users/suhaan/devenv --since 7d' (read-only) — dump the output and identify the printed savings assumption verbatim.
6. Binary size / startup: report 'time entire graph version' and the binary size; note that the checked-in binary is 75MB and say what accounts for it if you can tell (grammars linked in? cgo?). Check with 'otool -L' / 'go version -m' whether it is cgo-linked and what modules it embeds.`,
  },
]

const verdicts = await parallel(VERIFIERS.map(v => () =>
  agent(VPRE + v.prompt, { label: `verify:${v.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERIFY_SCHEMA })
))

return {
  notes: notes.filter(Boolean),
  verification: verdicts.filter(Boolean),
  missing_readers: AREAS.filter((_, i) => !notes[i]).map(a => a.key),
  missing_verifiers: VERIFIERS.filter((_, i) => !verdicts[i]).map(v => v.key),
}

57	
58	Everything is **deterministic** (pure tree-sitter static analysis — no LLM, no vectors, no similarity thresholds), **git-native** (every result keyed by `(repo, commit, tree)`, so it is content-addressed and cacheable per commit), and **100% local** (no keys, no network, no telemetry). It scales to millions of relations on one machine and releases memory after each build.
59	
60	---
61	
62	## 🚀 Install
63	
64	**Prerequisites:** the Entire CLI · Git · a Go toolchain with **CGO enabled** (tree-sitter uses native parser bindings).
65	
66	```sh
67	# 1. Install the plugin binary and register it with Entire's managed plugin dir
68	go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-graph@main
69	entire plugin install "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/entire-graph" --force
70	
71	# 2. Verify the install and the local-only environment
72	entire graph version
73	entire graph doctor --json        # includes "no_egress": true
74	
75	# 3. Run your first semantic diff, from any git repository
76	entire graph commit HEAD
77	```
78	
79	Entire plugins are local executables, not a hosted marketplace: `entire graph` works because Entire finds an `entire-graph` binary in its managed plugin directory or on `$PATH`. If `$(go env GOPATH)/bin` is already on your `PATH`, Entire can discover the binary directly after `go install`.
80	
81	### 🛠️ Install from source
82	
83	```sh
84	git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph.git
85	cd entire-graph
86	mise run build                        # go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph
87	entire plugin install ./entire-graph --force
88	```
89	
90	`scripts/install-local.sh` does this in one command (builds, installs, prints `entire graph version`, and fails early if the parent `entire` CLI is not on `PATH`). For release archives with `SHA256SUMS`, run `scripts/release.sh`. See [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md) for target and cgo details.
91	
92	### 🔄 Updating (and migrating from `entire-sem`)
93	
94	This plugin was renamed from `entire-sem` to `entire-graph` after `v0.1.0` — both the binary and the `cmd/` path changed. To update, or to switch over from the old `entire-sem`:
95	
96	```sh
97	go install github.com/entireio/entire-graph/cmd/entire-graph@latest
98	entire plugin install "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/entire-graph" --force
99	rm -f "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/entire-sem"   # remove the old binary if you had it
100	```
101	
102	> `…/cmd/entire-graph@latest` needs **v0.2.0 or newer** — `v0.1.0` predates the rename and only ships `cmd/entire-sem`, so `@latest` against it fails with *"module found (v0.1.0), but does not contain package …/cmd/entire-graph"*. If a fresh tag hasn't propagated to the Go module proxy yet, pin it (`@v0.2.0`) or use `@main`. Graph and query behavior is unchanged — only the name.
103	
104	---
105	
106	## 🔌 MCP & Entire Brain integration
107	
108	**entire-graph is not itself an MCP server, and it exposes no MCP tools.** It is a local CLI plugin and a machine-readable **semantic provider**. There is nothing to configure as an MCP endpoint here, and no daemon to run.
109	
110	MCP access to code intelligence comes from **Entire Brain** (`entire-brain`), a **separate** downstream product. Entire Brain ingests entire-graph's NDJSON output (`snapshot` / `symbols` / `edges`) into its own persistent store and is what exposes MCP tools to agents (`brain_search`, `brain_code`, `brain_impact`, `brain_context`, and so on). So the split is:
111	
112	| Layer | Role | How you use it |
113	|---|---|---|
114	| **entire-graph** (this repo) | Deterministic graph engine + NDJSON provider | `entire graph <command>` on the CLI (see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)) |
115	| **Entire Brain** (separate) | Persistence, indexing, query, **MCP server** | MCP tools in your agent, backed by the graph above |
116	
117	If you want MCP-style querying inside an agent, install and configure **Entire Brain** (its own docs) — entire-graph is the graph it builds on. If you just want direct, no-egress graph queries from an agent or the terminal, call `entire graph ...` directly; no MCP layer is required.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## ♻️ Refresh & keeping the graph current
122	
123	entire-graph has **no watch mode, no daemon, and no file-watcher**, and it needs none. The graph is **deterministic and content-addressed by `(repo, commit, tree)`**, so "refreshing" is just re-running a query — the result reflects whatever state you point it at.
124	
125	There are two modes, and neither can go stale on you:
126	
127	- **Working tree (default).** Every `search`, `neighbors`, and `snapshot` re-reads your live files, so results always include your uncommitted edits. Nothing to refresh — just run the command again.
128	- **Committed tree (`--head`).** Results are cached by the git **tree hash**. The cache directory defaults to the platform's per-user cache directory (`~/Library/Caches/entire-graph` on macOS, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/entire-graph` or `~/.cache/entire-graph` elsewhere); `--cache-dir` and `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` override it, in that order. Make a new commit and the tree hash changes, so the cache **automatically misses and rebuilds** — you can never read a committed-tree answer that is stale for that commit. `--no-cache` disables the cache entirely. Caching only ever changes latency, never results: measured on this repository, a cold `--head --profile full` search is 9.2s wall and the same query warm is 1.0s, with output byte-identical to `--no-cache`.
129	
130	To warm the cache for a large repo before a latency-sensitive session, prebuild it once:
131	
132	```sh
133	entire graph index --repo . --head --profile full --cache-dir /path/to/cache
134	```
135	
136	Re-running `index` **is** the refresh: same tree → instant cache hit; changed tree → a fresh build. After that, `search` and `neighbors` on the same committed tree report the cache hit directly. This is the whole "keep it current" story — deterministic re-index, no background process.
137

162

164	|---|---|
165	| `entire graph search --query "..."` | 🔍 Ranked source regions for a natural-language task |
166	| `entire graph neighbors --symbol NAME_OR_ID` | Callers / callees / relations for one symbol (impact) |
167	| `entire graph symbols --format ndjson` | Full stream of symbol definitions |
168	| `entire graph edges --format ndjson` | Full stream of relations (all 30 types) |
169	| `entire graph snapshot --format ndjson` | 🕸️ Full graph: header + files + symbols + relations |
170	| `entire graph commit <rev>` | Entity-level semantic diff of a commit vs its first parent |
171	| `entire graph diff --base <a> --head <b>` | Semantic diff between two refs (`analyze` is an alias) |
172	| `entire graph checkpoint <id>` | Semantic diff for the commit behind an Entire checkpoint trailer |
173	| `entire graph index --head` | Prebuild / warm the durable committed-tree cache |
174	| `entire graph capabilities --json` | Languages, relation types, features, network requirements |
175	| `entire graph doctor --json` | Environment, repo resolution, plugin data dir, `no_egress=true` |
176	| `entire graph version [--json]` | Provider name and plugin version |
177	
178	### 🔍 How `search` ranks (file-class prior + duplicate collapsing)
179	
180	`search` answers a *code* question: the caller's next action is an edit to a source file. Two
181	classes of result are systematically over-scored by a body-text match and almost never the edit
182	site, so both are corrected explicitly:
183	
184	| Class | Examples | Prior |
185	|---|---|---|
186	| source | `src/**`, headers, any parsed language file | `1.0` |
187	| documentation | `.md` `.mdx` `.rst` `.adoc` `.txt`, `docs/`, `website/`, `versioned_docs/`, README, CHANGELOG, man pages | `0.5` |
188	| vendored | `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `third_party/`, `site-packages/` | `0.5` |
189	| generated | `dist/`, `generated/`, `single_include/`, `*-lock.json`, `Cargo.lock` | `0.5` |
190	| example | `examples/`, `samples/`, `demo/` | `0.75` |
191	
192	The prior is a **multiplier on the positive part of a hit's score, never a filter**. `0.5` means
193	"a documentation hit has to be twice as relevant as the best source hit to outrank it" — a doc
194	still ranks first when it is genuinely the only match, and the prior is switched off completely
195	when the query itself asks for that class (`documentation`, `readme`, `changelog`, `example`,
196	`dist`, `vendored`, …). Demoted hits are labelled `doc-prior` / `vendored-prior` /
197	`generated-prior` / `example-prior` in `signals`.
198	
199	**Near-duplicate collapsing.** Repositories carry deliberate copies of the same content —
200	versioned documentation trees (`version-2.x/x` beside `version-3.0.1/x`), vendored snapshots,
201	generated mirrors — and every copy scores identically, so one document can consume the whole
202	result budget. Copies are merged into the best-ranked one, which reports a `+N similar` signal;
203	the freed slots go to genuinely different code. Collapsing requires distinct files with the same
204	basename, outside different monorepo units, and either identical normalized region text or
205	paths equal modulo version-like segments with ≥ 90% token overlap.
206	
207	Full flags and the agent-facing operating guide are in **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)**. Diff commands print human-readable text by default and structured output with `--json`:
208	
209	When a neighbor lookup by name is ambiguous, each definition is listed with the
210	narrowest selector that picks it out — `--symbol NAME --file <path> --line <n>`,
211	plus `--kind <kind>` when two records share a name and a line. Copy that
212	selector verbatim.
213	
214	`--symbol` also accepts a definition's stable `compound-v1` ID
215	(`repoKey:language:path:kind:qualifiedName`, with a `#sig:` suffix for
216	overloads), which `symbols --format ndjson` emits. An exact ID match wins over
217	every other filter — it already encodes the file and kind, so a stale `--file`
218	cannot veto it — and it is the one selector that survives edits shifting line
219	numbers. The ambiguity listing prints selectors rather than IDs because an ID
220	repeats the path and name the same line already shows.
221	
222	```text
223	Semantic changes HEAD~1..HEAD
224	
225	auth.py
226	  ~ function validate_token signature changed (14 dependents)
227	  + class TokenClaims added
228	  - function parse_token removed (0 dependents)
229	```

233	## 🗣️ Language support
234	
235	`capabilities --json` exposes two honest tiers: `semantic_languages` (parser-backed call/type/data-flow analysis) and `inventory_only_languages` (stable file/document records, no semantic claims). Current counts: **185 recognized names, 36 semantic, 149 inventory-only.**
236	
237	**36 semantic languages:** Bash, C, C#, C++, CUE, Clojure, ClojureScript, Dart, Elixir, Erlang, F#, Go, Groovy, HCL/Terraform, Haskell, Java, JavaScript, Julia, Kotlin, Lua, OCaml, Objective-C, PHP, Perl, Protocol Buffers, Python, R, Ruby, Rust, SQL, Scala, Swift, TypeScript, YAML (including GitHub Actions workflow sections and jobs), Zig, Zsh.

239	Everything else is reported as an honest partial failure rather than dropped silently. See [docs/language-support.md](docs/language-support.md) for the full two-tier matrix.

285	---
286	
287	## ⚡ Performance
288	
289	- **Semantic diff:** about 0.1s for a typical `HEAD~1..HEAD` on redis.
290	- **Full-graph build:** linear in repository size; 23K relations in 1.5s up to 2.27M relations in 25.6s across the repos above.
291	- **Streaming output:** `snapshot` emits records as it parses, so memory stays bounded on very large repositories.
292	- **Cached committed-tree search:** reuses a tree-keyed compressed index across invocations, in the platform's per-user cache directory unless `--cache-dir`/`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` redirect it, so repeated queries on an unchanged tree skip re-parsing. The working tree is never cached. A complete prepared index derives the exact query-selected view, so relation expansion cannot escape that file set.
293	- **Explicit preindex:** `index --head` builds and verifies that query-independent artifact before latency-sensitive work; cached `search` and `neighbors` calls then report the hit directly.
294	
295	Absolute numbers are environment-sensitive (measured on Apple Silicon). Read them as relative signals and reproduce locally with the harness.
296	
297	---
298	
299	## 🔒 Security & local-first
300	
301	- **Zero egress.** No API keys, no network calls, no telemetry, no grammar downloads at runtime. All 36 grammars are vendored and compiled in.
302	- **Verifiable.** `entire graph doctor --json` reports `no_egress=true`. Pass `--no-network` to make the no-egress contract explicit to callers.
303	- **Writes only to Entire's managed plugin directory.** Your code is read locally and never leaves the machine — safe to point at private repositories.
304	- **Reads committed `HEAD` by default** for provider/graph streams; pass `--worktree` to include live edits.
305	
306	---
307	
308	## 🏗️ Architecture
309	
310	```text
311	cmd/
312	  entire-graph/     Plugin entry point (semantic diff, search, provider commands)
313	  graph-bench/      Reproducible benchmark driver
314	internal/
315	  cli/              Hand-rolled command dispatch and flag parsing
316	  sem/              Tree-sitter parsing, symbol + relation extraction, rename reconciliation, search
317	  gitutil/          Git subprocess wrappers (NUL-delimited output parsing)
318	  bench/            Measurement core (throughput, memory, coverage)
319	docs/               Language support matrix, benchmarks, operations, provider requirements, ADRs
320	scripts/            Local install and checksum-backed release archives
321	```
322	
323	The parser is isolated behind `internal/sem`, so the command surface stays stable while the semantic model gets richer. The wire schema is a frozen `1.x` GA contract (additive-only minors; see `docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`).
324	
325	---
326	
327	## ⚠️ Current limits
328	
329	- Dependent counts are heuristic, not compiler / type-checker accurate.
330	- `CALLS`, `HANDLES_ROUTE`, and `HANDLES_TOOL` relations are heuristic.
331	- Rename detection is heuristic.
332	- Unsupported languages are reported as partial failures, not parsed semantically.
333	- The plugin is invoked as `entire graph ...`; it requires no changes to the main Entire CLI.

entire-graph DOES cache working-tree searches (content-digest key, `gitutil.WorktreeContentDigest`),

Measured 2026-08-08:

- `devenv/entire.io`: 30 dirty paths, no untracked dirs → caches fine, 4501ms → 67ms (67x).
- Synthetic repo: 1 untracked file → caches. 100-file untracked dir → never caches.

**Why:** a workflow/subagent run that leaves worktrees behind silently converts the repo it ran in
into a permanently uncached one. Latency looks like "the tool is slow", not "the cache is off".

`git status --porcelain -uall | grep '/$'` for untracked dirs and clean up `.claude/worktrees/`.

one is about the key being tree-keyed not binary-keyed; this one is about the key never being
computed at all.

content.text:
# entire-graph, end to end

## The one-sentence model

It is a **75 MB static tree-sitter analyzer with no network, no model, and no daemon** that turns a git tree into a symbol+relation graph, and then spends most of its ~62k lines of engine code not on the graph but on **packing a search answer into an agent's context window**.

That framing matters: `internal/sem` is 62k LOC, and roughly a third of it (`search_*.go`, ~30 files) exists purely to decide *what text an agent gets and what it must give up to get it*. The graph is the substrate; the payload budget is the product.

---

## 1. Shape

```
entire (parent CLI, 62 MB)          ← contains ZERO graph code
  └─ execs: ~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-graph  (75 MB)
       cmd/entire-graph/main.go     21 lines → cli.Execute()
       internal/cli/    10k LOC     hand-rolled switch, no cobra, exit codes 0/1 only
       internal/sem/    62k LOC     parse · graph · resolve · search
       internal/gitutil 1.2k LOC    git subprocess wrappers
```

`entire graph …` is kubectl-style dispatch by name — the parent prepends the managed plugin dir to `PATH` and execs the binary with `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`/`ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`/`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`. `entire-plugin.yml` is dead metadata; nothing parses it.

**One Go dependency**: `smacker/go-tree-sitter`. 20 grammars from that module, 13 more vendored as raw C (`internal/sem/grammars/`, plus `pgsql/` and `zsh/`). I verified the size: `__TEXT.__const` alone is 63.1 MB — 80.3% of the binary — and symbol-level attribution puts **84.9% in `_ts_parse_table`/`ts_*`**. All compiled Go and C code together is 7.1 MB. The grammars *are* the binary. It still starts in ~6 ms (mmap'd, not faulted); the 26.7 ms you see for `entire graph version` is ~20 ms of parent-CLI dispatch.

**Local-only is real, and I checked it three ways.** Zero `net/http`, `crypto/tls`, `net.Dial`, `net.Listen`, `net.(*Resolver)` symbols in the worker (positive control: the parent CLI has 1862/731/1). All 10 verbs run to correct completion under `sandbox-exec (deny network*)` where `curl` fails rc=6. No `net`/`net/http` import anywhere in the 111 non-test source files. Caveat: `doctor`'s `no_egress: true` is a **hardcoded literal**, not a probe — it documents intent. And one real hatch exists: `entire graph verify` runs `sh -c <your string>`, which will happily `go test` its way onto the network. That verb isn't reachable from search and isn't even in the installed build.

---

## 2. The pipeline: tree → graph

**Discovery.** Worktree mode: `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` so *git* owns the exclude stack. `--head`: `git ls-tree -r` at a pinned commit resolved in two steps (`rev-parse HEAD` then `^{tree}`) so provenance can't mix if HEAD moves. Fallback is a `WalkDir` with a nested-.gitignore stack and a hand-rolled glob engine — which, notably, has **no character-class support** (`*.[oa]` never matches what git matches).

**Routing.** Path first (special basenames → multi-dot suffix → extension), then shebang (1 KiB prefix, `env` indirection, version-suffix stripping), then content sniffs (`.h` → Objective-C vs C++, `.js` → Flow/TSX).

**Two honest tiers**, and `capabilities --json` matches `docs/language-support.md` with a zero-element set diff in both directions (I had that checked): **185 recognized / 36 semantic / 149 inventory-only**.

**Parsing is tree-sitter plus a large hand-rolled layer** — this is the part the docs undersell:

- **Byte-length-preserving masks** run *before* tree-sitter so offsets computed on masked source can be sliced from the original. C/C++ masks emulate a preprocessor; TypeScript masks syntax the grammar can't handle; Rust unwraps `cfg_*!{}` item wrappers with up to 8 extra full parses.
- **Groovy has no grammar at all** — the best available one produced 1,400+ errors on apache/groovy, so it's a fully hand-rolled structural scanner.
- **YAML is parsed and the AST thrown away** — the tree is used only to set `HasError()`; symbols come from a line/indent scanner.
- 13 grammar-less filetypes (JSON, Markdown, TOML, XML, Make, Dockerfile…) get regex fallback extractors.
- C/C++ at non-`full` profiles bypass tree-sitter entirely for a regex scanner.

Explicit `parser.Close()`/`tree.Close()` is load-bearing: leaving the cgo objects to finalizers measured **12+ GB RSS** on microsoft/TypeScript, because the Go heap stays small so GC rarely runs.

**Symbol identity** is `compound-v1` = `repoKey:language:path:kind:qualifiedName`, with `#sig:<16-hex>` + ordinal only on in-file collision. Byte ranges exist internally but are **deliberately never serialized**, so IDs survive line shifts.

---

## 3. The graph model

30 relation types in a frozen list — `DEFINES CONTAINS IMPORTS CALLS CONSTRUCTS ASYNC_CALLS EXTENDS INHERITS IMPLEMENTS OVERRIDES USES_TYPE PARAM_TYPE RETURNS_TYPE READS_FIELD WRITES_FIELD ACCESSES HANDLES_ROUTE HANDLES_GRPC HANDLES_GRAPHQL HANDLES_TRPC HTTP_CALLS EMITS LISTENS_ON HANDLES_TOOL CONFIGURES SIMILAR_TO TESTS RESOURCE_DEPENDS_ON DATA_FLOWS FILE_CHANGES_WITH` — of which **7 are flagged heuristic**. Schema frozen at 1.1, additive-only (ADR 0001).

Every edge carries `confidence`, `resolution` (exact / package / import_resolved / import_external / name_only / type_inferred / pattern / git_history), `relation_scope`, `target_kind`, and optional call-site `evidence`. Profiles gate the set: **syntax-only = 2 relations, fast = 9, full = 30**.

**Determinism is airtight for the streams.** Two independent cold builds into separate cache dirs produced byte-identical 36,361-record edge streams; cold output equals warm output exactly. (One exception found: `commit --json` produced four distinct hashes across five runs on an unchanged tree — map-iteration order in `compareEntities`.)

---

## 4. Resolution — the genuinely hard part

Call-site → definition binding is a **name-based tier ladder, ambiguity-averse by design**:

```
same-file exact            0.92
import-bound               0.86
Go same-package unique     0.80   (pathProximityRank: same file 0, same dir 1, …)
workspace-unique name      0.68
```

**First tier that produces a result wins; a tier with >1 candidate usually returns nothing.** Four exceptions fan out: same-file multi-def → lexically nearest, imported multi → all at 0.62 relabelled `name_only`, PHP → top-4 by size at 0.55, C/C++ same-file overload sets at 0.62.

Two Go-specific mechanisms are worth knowing: package scoping by path proximity (so a name reused per sibling package binds locally), and **structural interface satisfaction** — a call landing on an interface requirement is carried to every satisfying concrete type, capped at 8. That satisfaction check is **method-name sets only, no signature or arity check**.

What is deliberately *not* resolved: recursion (self-calls are unconditionally suppressed), dynamic dispatch, reflection, `getattr`, DI containers, C++ template specializations (handled only as search aliases). Call sites are a **set of names per symbol body**, not a list — ten calls to the same function collapse to one edge, and evidence points at the caller's whole span, not the call line.

And a naming trap: `dependents_count` in `diff`/`commit` is **not** a graph count. It's a lexical token-occurrence scan over entity blocks — a type annotation or a bare mention counts.

---

## 5. Search — the actual product

```
preselect files → score candidates → (optional BM25 fusion) → dedupe/prior
  → select → fit to budget → allocate bodies → assemble blocks
```

**Preselection** never indexes the whole repo. Default pool is `min(256, max(96, topK*3))` — which is why I saw `files_indexed=96` for both a 412-file Go repo and a 1918-file TS repo. Three backends: `git-tree-grep` (committed, preindexed), `git-index-grep+go-content` (worktree, ≥10k files), or plain content scan. The source comment records the measurement that *wider pools hurt recall*.

**Scoring** (`scoreSearchCandidates`, search.go:2546) is BM25 plus hand-tuned structural terms:

```go
score = base + bm25 + 7*coverage + min(24, codeTokenBonus) + structuralAdjustment
        + 2 if coverage == 1
```

with `codeTokenBonus += 6*weight` per code-like term, and structural adjustments of `+3` executable / `−3` container / `+4` name-covers-query / `+8` two code terms in the qualified name / **`+15` for a dotted call mention** (`Type.method()` in the query names the fix site outright). Unmatched query terms contribute **zero, never a penalty** — a word the repo has never heard of must not tax documents that matched the rest.

**Path priors** are multiplicative demotions, switched off when the query asks for that class: tests `−12`, docs `−6`, generated `−6`, `.github/` non-workflow `−12`, third_party `−5`. The comments carry the measurements that set them ("was −1.5 — far too weak"; a test file matching the issue's exact tokens scores 26–47 while the implementation sits at 13).

**"Semantic" means structural, not vectors.** There is no embedding model. The "semantic" pool is lexical+graph-expanded; `--deep` adds an exhaustive BM25 sparse pass and fuses it. Measured: `--deep` costs +23% wall and reads 3.6× more bytes for an **unchanged top hit** — and it has two real defects (three result slots spent on the same `symbol_id` at overlapping spans, and output not sorted by score).

**Payload assembly** is where the real engineering is. One ceiling (`--max-context-bytes`, default 24576), and the body allocator is a *search over demotion plans*: for each "demote from rank K", score `Σ1/rank` for complete bodies + `0.25/rank` for windows, take max value then min size. The tail pays before the growth allowance. Blocks, in order:

| block | what it replaces |
|---|---|
| CLOSED SET | the read that discovers a switch you forgot to extend |
| ranked hits (complete bodies for the head) | the follow-up file read |
| COVERING TEST + ALSO COVERING | "what has to keep passing" |
| VERIFY | a fumbled test invocation |
| SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL | a repo-wide grep |
| RELATED SITES | the sibling/caller you'd have patched second |

VERIFY walks up to 32 ancestor dirs across 10 ecosystem derivations in fixed order (cargo → go → maven → gradle → node → composer → pytest → ruby → cmake → make), degrading narrow → suite → build-check → a 96-byte "none derivable" floor that can never be silent. It works: I saw `cd frontend && npx vitest run <path>` derived from `frontend/package.json` on the TS repo and `go test ./internal/sem -run '^TestX$'` from `go.mod` on the Go one.

The three **reference blocks are off by default** because six real-agent runs measured them as pure cost (+2.1 turns, +14–19% cost, resolves flat-to-worse). The discriminator the code applies is *"does this block replace a tool call?"* — they don't.

---

## 6. Caching — and the thing I'd fix first

Two gzip'd disk caches under one root (`--cache-dir` > `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` > `~/Library/Caches/entire-graph`). Key = sha256 over cache version, abs repo path, repo key, provider version, **git tree hash**, profile, parse caps, `OnlyFiles`, and ignore-file paths *and contents*. Commit is not in the key — amends and content-neutral rebases hit, and the loaded commit is re-stamped.

Incrementality is **whole-tree only**. One character → new tree hash → full rebuild.

Two traps, one of which I confirmed live and which directly affects your benchmark work:

**(a) The cache is tree-keyed, not binary-keyed in practice.** `providerVersion` *is* in the key, but `mise run build` is a bare `go build` with no `-ldflags`, so every local build keys as `"dev"`. Two different binaries share one cache. (You already have this as `eg-ab-testing-cache-trap`.)

**(b) `.claude/worktrees/` silently disables caching in this very repo.** Two of my agents disagreed on whether the default worktree path caches at all, so I tested it myself. The truth: dirty worktrees **are** cached via a content digest, up to `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` differing paths — but an untracked *directory* is walked file-by-file against that same budget, and a nested git repo shows as **one** `git status` entry while containing thousands of files.

```
entire-graph  17 nested agent worktrees = 6,195 files  →  cache_hit=false forever, ~5.0s/search
entire.io     30 dirty paths, no dirs    →  4501ms → 67ms  (67x)
synthetic     1 untracked file           →  caches
              1 nested git repo          →  never caches
```

So workflow runs that leave worktrees behind convert the repo they ran in into a permanently uncached one, and it reads as "the tool is slow." `--head` sidesteps it. I've saved this to memory.

Also worth knowing: `neighbors`/`impact`/`def` default to **worktree**, so on a repo in state (b) every interactive query pays the full rebuild. And the cache has **no eviction, no TTL, no GC** — yours is at 972 entries / 406 MB including two abandoned version directories.

---

## 7. Verbs, honestly

Solid: `search`, `impact` (six sections, co-change genuinely from `git log` over a bounded recent window — I cross-checked the counts), `symbols`/`edges`/`snapshot` (disciplined schemas, deterministic), `index --report` (byte-identical across runs), `capabilities`, `diff`/`commit`.

Rough edges found by execution, not reading:

- **`neighbors --depth 2` is a no-op** — depth-1 and depth-2 payloads are byte-identical after stripping latency fields. `impact` *does* traverse transitively (with `via` attribution); it's just not wired into `neighbors`.
- **`neighbors` with no `--relation` silently means CALLS only**, and an invalid relation name is accepted with rc=0 and zero results. Two ways to get a confident wrong answer.
- **In JSON, ambiguity isn't an error** — `disambiguation_required: true` with *empty* `incoming`/`outgoing`. A consumer reading only `matches[].incoming` sees "zero callers." Text/agent formats handle it well and print a working selector.
- **`--format` changes the result set, not just the encoding**: at 2048 bytes, JSON returns 2 hits and agent returns 10 — agent buys them by dropping VERIFY and SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL that JSON keeps.
- Result count is **non-monotonic** in `--max-context-bytes` (2 → 5 → 11 → 10 → 10) and **saturates at the 24576 default** — the flag can shrink output but never grow it.
- Your installed plugin binary (2026-08-02) and the repo build (2026-08-08) produce **different graphs from the identical tree** — 7370 vs 7372 symbols — and both report version `"dev"`.

## 8. The evidence story

This is the part I'd want you to hear straight, since it's your campaign.

The docs are internally split. `README.md` is current and **withdraws every end-to-end token-savings claim**. `docs/DETAILS.md` is the *old* README, still shipping 54.9%/57.7%, "94% on 21 repos", "283x", and peak-memory-vs-competitor tables — and asserts they're all reproducible with `cmd/graph-bench`, which **has no scoring harness and knows nothing about competitors**. ---

# STATE REPORT — graph-bench estate, 2026-08-08 ~23:55 UTC

**Headline:** no graph-bench process is running anywhere. rep50 completed 196/196 twenty-three hours ago. rep50 is **not** a holdout and never was — it was contaminated at birth and has since been used to select code. Three of the project's four "held-out" sets are burned. The single copy of every August result sits on a preemptible VM with no backup, and its two siblings were already preempted.

---

## A. Repository inventory

**84 git roots under `devenv/`; 41 top-level (16 clones, 25 worktrees).** The benchmark-relevant ones:

| path | kind | branch | HEAD | vs origin/main | dirty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `devenv/graphmark` | clone | `graph-savings-iterate` | `623b2c62` 07-29 | −9 / +89 | 6 tracked (incl. `tools/run_3arm.sh`, `tools/eg-q`), 842 untracked |
| **`~/graphmark-bench`** | clone | `fix/cmm-arm-revival-and-cache-isolation` | `1075f1d9` | +10 | — |
| `devenv/entire-graph` | clone | `fix/graph-retrieval-and-typescript` | `0c40355` 08-08 | −34 / +27 | 34 untracked |
| `devenv/entire-graph` **local `main`** | — | `main` | `114e1788` 07-28 | −130 / +6 | — |
| `entire-graph-{gate,statusline}`, `eg-{consolidated,rank35,turnkill,measure-turnkill}` | worktrees of `devenv/entire-graph` | various | — | −44…−156 | mostly clean |
| `devenv/cmm` | **not a repo** | — | dangling symlink | — | target missing |

**`devenv/graphmark` is not the harness that ran the campaign.** `~/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/tools/run_3arm.sh` is 2579 lines with 4 arms; the devenv copy is 1083 lines with 3 arms and zero `PUBLISHED_EXACT`. Anything quoted from "graphmark" must name which tree.

**PRs.** graphmark #7–#66: 30 merged / 28 closed / **2 open (#54, #56 — ashtom's, confirmed do-not-merge)**. entire-graph #19–#87: 47 merged / 11 closed / **2 open (#86, #87, both yours, opened 2026-08-07T20:35Z)**. origin/main = `8f6764d6`. `AGENT-COMMS.md:173` "do not merge #84" is stale — #84 merged 2026-08-07T19:45:40Z (`2d565cc8`).

**Binary attribution per run — this is broken, and it is the worst finding in section A.**

- Of 3,271 eg-arm sessions locally, **2,697 record no binary at all**; 574 record only a path; **10** record a sha.
- Every path they name (`/tmp/graphmark-bin/eg-measure`, `eg-frozen`, `eg-integ-measure-2026-07-28`, `eg-notice2`) **has been deleted**.
- Every surviving binary reports `version=dev` — `entire-graph/mise.toml:27` has no `-ldflags`, `cmd/entire-graph/main.go:14` `var version = "dev"`.
- Four binaries stamp `vcs.revision=99123e0dad4a`, which is **devenv's** HEAD, an object that does not exist in entire-graph. `tool_identity.json` records that wrong sha in all 27 cases.
- `run_3arm.sh:28-32` FATALs on `version=dev`, yet all three eg binaries on graphbench-c report `dev` and 250 `eg-q.run` files prove sessions ran. The guard did not hold.
- No sha-pinned binary exists on this machine; `bin/entire-graph-94009ef` (cited in memory) is not present anywhere.
- `9552d4c` is a **graphmark** commit, not entire-graph, and lives only on unmerged remote branches.

**Conclusion: no existing cohort can be attributed to a specific entire-graph build.** Cross-cohort comparison is unsupported. (One mitigation: the search cache key hashes `absRepo`, which embeds the run tag, so cross-*tag* cache bleed did not occur.)

---

## B. Benchmark inventory

**Dataset.** `swe-bench/SWE-bench_Multilingual` test split, 300 instances, 9 languages — Ruby 44, Java 43, Rust 43, PHP 43, Go 42, JavaScript 33, C 30, C++ 12, TypeScript 10. Python enters only via 3 SWE-bench-Verified rows (plus 10 SWE-bench-Pro rows in rep50).

**Repetitions: one.** All 77 live tags are `*_r1_*`; 1258/1298 job lines carry `rep=1`.

**Selection.** 34–40 `.elig_*.txt` lists. Only the `.elig_gate_{5,10,20,30,60,300}` family is seed-frozen with a sha256 manifest (SEED=20260729, 155 banned across 20 historical tuning files). **`.elig_gate_300.txt` holds 146 ids, not 300.** `.elig_strat60`=50, `.elig_prereg30`=29, `.elig_prereg100`=99.

**Model/effort.** Set in driver env, not the runner. 27 `tools/*.sh` set `CC_MODEL=opus`; `CC_MAX_TURNS=120`, `CC_TIMEOUT=3600`. **All 28 handoff-config workers export `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, which nothing in `tools/` reads** — the runner reads `CC_EFFORT`. So RUNG1/RUNG2*/O35*/PUB/HAIKU30/FIXSTACK likely ran at CLI-default effort while `tools/run_*.sh` cells passed `--effort max|high`. **Effort is an uncontrolled between-cohort variable.** Unresolved — verifying needs `claude --help`, barred by the gate.

**Arms.** baseline | eg | cmm | graphify. Gate for a scored pair: `usd>0 AND non-empty patch.diff` (`metrics.py:152-154`), degenerates excluded from token stats but kept in resolve denominators.

## C. Existing result inventory

**Grading has not been run for 338 of 378 cohorts.** For nearly every cohort the gate is "produced a patch," not "resolved." Where grading exists it is untrustworthy:

- `rg29*` vs `scr30*` graded **byte-identical** patch sets and disagree: eg 19/27 vs 11/27 (8 flips), cmm 19/27 vs 12/27, baseline 17/25 vs 16/25. The disagreement is larger than most reported effects.
- **REP50 grading is broken**: `grade4c` exit=0 but completed_ids = baseline 39 / eg 3 / cmm 0 / graphify 0, resolved 36/3/0/0. No 4-arm resolve rate is derivable.
- `README.md:88`'s "27/30 both arms, Δ0" for the sonnet pilot has **no surviving grading artifact**.

**rep50 — raw, all 49, no post-outcome filter** (extracted live by me from `graphbench-c:~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench/results/REP50_r1_*`):

| arm | n | succ | patch | total tok | input | cache-create | cache-read | output | USD | turns | wall s | graph calls |

Two things this table makes visible that the published figures hide. **95.5% of "total tokens" is cache-read** — the headline metric is essentially a cache-read metric. And these are `usage.*` fields, which graphmark commit `3876d46c` (2026-07-28) declared lossy and replaced with `modelUsage`; `sc50.py` (written 2026-08-07 20:34) reads `usage.*` anyway. `PLAN-TO-35PCT.md:37` reports graphify −0.50%; raw all-49 is −6.76%. The −0.50% survives only by dropping graphify's one non-success while keeping all 49 baseline sessions.

**Invalid/missing cells (local):** 7,480 session dirs → 7,204 non-empty `cc_out.json`, 38 zero-byte, 238 missing (130 alt-format), **108 genuinely empty**; 1 corrupt (`t3g/cmm/caddyserver__caddy-4774`). 205 zero-byte `patch.diff`. input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# READ-ONLY w.r.t. source: copies only, never modifies/deletes anything under $HOME/work or $HOME.
# Writes exclusively into a fresh /tmp staging dir.
set -uo pipefail

TS=20260809t0055z
STAGE=/tmp/gmpreserve-$TS
SRC_HOME=$HOME
S=$HOME/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
OUT=$STAGE/graphbench-c-metadata
mkdir -p "$OUT" "$STAGE"

CAND=$STAGE/candidates.txt
: > "$CAND"

# ---------- 1. CANDIDATE ALLOWLIST (explicit; no globs into bulk trees) ----------
# home-level scripts / logs / small json+md (top level only)
find "$SRC_HOME" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
  \( -name '*.py' -o -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.log' -o -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.json' \) \
  >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# suite top-level: eligibility selectors, manifests, launchers, docs
find "$S" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
  \( -name '.elig_*' -o -name '*.json' -o -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.log' \) \
  >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# tools/ and tasks/ in full (scoring scripts, runners, cohort manifests)
find "$S/tools" "$S/tasks" -type f >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# analysis/ + measure/ if present (derived scoring outputs)
find "$S/analysis" "$S/measure" -type f -size -2M >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# per-session metadata ONLY (never checkouts/graphs/repo-cache)
find "$S/results" -maxdepth 4 -type f \
  \( -name 'cc_out.json' -o -name 'cc_err.log' -o -name 'patch.diff' -o -name 'prompt.txt' \
     -o -name 'tool_identity.json' -o -name 'gq_calls.log' -o -name 'gq_calls.log.payload' \
     -o -name '*-q.run' -o -name 'usage.json' -o -name 'provision.log' \
     -o -name 'preds.json' -o -name '*_eval.json' \) >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# result-tree top-level indexes / logs / reports
find "$S/results" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.md' -o -name '*.log' -o -name '*.json' \) -size -8M >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

sort -u "$CAND" -o "$CAND"
echo "CANDIDATES_RAW=$(wc -l < "$CAND")"

# ---------- 2. NAME-BASED SECRET EXCLUSION ----------
NAMEX=$STAGE/excluded_by_name.txt
KEEP1=$STAGE/keep1.txt
grep -Ei '(^|/)(\.claude\.json|\.claude\.json\.tmp[^/]*|\.netrc|\.git-credentials|authorized_keys|known_hosts)$|(^|/)\.ssh/|(^|/)\.config/gcloud/|\.env($|\.)|(^|/)[^/]*(credential|secret|token|passwd|password)[^/]*$|\.(pem|key|p12|pfx|jks|keystore)$|\.(tgz|tar|tar\.gz|zip|gz|whl|so|bin)$' \
  "$CAND" > "$NAMEX" 2>/dev/null
grep -Evi '(^|/)(\.claude\.json|\.claude\.json\.tmp[^/]*|\.netrc|\.git-credentials|authorized_keys|known_hosts)$|(^|/)\.ssh/|(^|/)\.config/gcloud/|\.env($|\.)|(^|/)[^/]*(credential|secret|token|passwd|password)[^/]*$|\.(pem|key|p12|pfx|jks|keystore)$|\.(tgz|tar|tar\.gz|zip|gz|whl|so|bin)$' \
  "$CAND" > "$KEEP1" 2>/dev/null
echo "EXCLUDED_BY_NAME=$(wc -l < "$NAMEX")"

# ---------- 3. CONTENT CREDENTIAL SCAN (filenames only; never prints matched text) ----------
CONTENTX=$STAGE/excluded_by_content.txt
KEEP2=$STAGE/keep2.txt
: > "$CONTENTX"
PAT='sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20}|gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{20}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20}|AIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30}|ya29\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20}|xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=.|OPENAI_API_KEY=.|GEMINI_API_KEY=.|FIREWORKS_API_KEY=.|"api_key"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]{12}|Authorization:[[:space:]]*Bearer[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20}'
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -r "$f" ] || continue
  if LC_ALL=C grep -aqE "$PAT" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then echo "$f" >> "$CONTENTX"; fi
done < "$KEEP1"
comm -23 "$KEEP1" <(sort -u "$CONTENTX") > "$KEEP2"
sort -u "$KEEP2" -o "$KEEP2"
echo "EXCLUDED_BY_CONTENT=$(wc -l < "$CONTENTX")"
echo "KEPT=$(wc -l < "$KEEP2")"

# ---------- 4. COPY (byte-for-byte, structure preserved) ----------
while IFS= read -r f; do
  rel="${f#/}"
  d="$OUT/$(dirname "$rel")"
  mkdir -p "$d"
  cp -a --no-preserve=ownership "$f" "$d/" 2>/dev/null
done < "$KEEP2"

# ---------- 5. INVENTORY + SHA-256 ----------
INV=$STAGE/INVENTORY.tsv
MAN=$STAGE/SHA256SUMS.txt
printf 'sha256\tsize_bytes\tmtime_utc\tarchive_path\n' > "$INV"
( cd "$OUT" && find . -type f -print0 | sort -z | while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
    h=$(sha256sum "$p" | awk '{print $1}')
    sz=$(stat -c %s "$p")
    mt=$(stat -c %y "$p" | cut -d. -f1)
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$h" "$sz" "$mt" "${p#./}" >> "$INV"
    printf '%s  %s\n' "$h" "${p#./}" >> "$MAN"
  done )
cp -a "$INV" "$MAN" "$NAMEX" "$CONTENTX" "$OUT/" 2>/dev/null

echo "FILES_ARCHIVED=$(( $(wc -l < "$INV") - 1 ))"
echo "BYTES_ARCHIVED=$(du -sb "$OUT" | awk '{print $1}')"

# ---------- 6. TARBALL ----------
TAR=$STAGE/graphmark-evidence-graphbench-c-$TS.tar.gz
tar -czf "$TAR" -C "$STAGE" "$(basename "$OUT")" 2>/dev/null
echo "TARBALL=$TAR"
echo "TARBALL_BYTES=$(stat -c %s "$TAR")"
echo "TARBALL_SHA256=$(sha256sum "$TAR" | awk '{print $1}')"
echo "STAGE=$STAGE"

import json,glob,os
R=os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench/results")
tot={"n":0,"mu_cost":0.0,"cost":0.0,"mu_tok":0,"us_tok":0,"mismatch":0,"lossy":0,"worst":0.0}
for arm in ["baseline","eg","cmm","graphify"]:
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{R}/REP50_r1_{arm}/{arm}/*/cc_out.json")):
        try: j=json.load(open(f))
        except Exception: continue
        u=j.get("usage") or {}; mu=j.get("modelUsage") or {}
        c=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0
        muc=sum((v or {}).get("costUSD",0) or 0 for v in mu.values())
        ut=sum(u.get(k,0) for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))
        mt=0
        for v in mu.values():
            v=v or {}
            mt+=sum(v.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        tot["n"]+=1; tot["cost"]+=c; tot["mu_cost"]+=muc; tot["us_tok"]+=ut; tot["mu_tok"]+=mt
        if c>0 and abs(muc-c)/c > 1e-9: tot["mismatch"]+=1
        if ut>0:
            r=mt/ut
            if r>1.05: tot["lossy"]+=1
            tot["worst"]=max(tot["worst"],r)
print(f"  rep50 sessions scanned         : {tot['n']}")
print(f"  sum(total_cost_usd)            : ${tot['cost']:.6f}")
print(f"  sum(modelUsage[*].costUSD)     : ${tot['mu_cost']:.6f}")

print(f"  usage.* total tokens           : {tot['us_tok']:,}")
print(f"  modelUsage total tokens        : {tot['mu_tok']:,}")
print(f"  modelUsage/usage ratio         : {tot['mu_tok']/tot['us_tok']:.6f}   sessions with ratio>1.05: {tot['lossy']}   worst: {tot['worst']:.2f}x")
