How the combined candidate was built

Two chains, zero shared patches

The #297 launch stack and the #298–#314 work were built separately on main. #315 cherry-picks the 106 absent commits onto #297, records a patch-equivalence ledger, and adds 8 composition commits.

Replay schema 6

#297 bound replay to the producer at schema 4. #306 used 4 for its off mode, a collision. Now: schema 6 for both modes, with the same producer, the same VERIFY mode, and schemas 0–5 refused.

Whole body first

A certified whole, unchanged body ([complete]) comes first, then the focus window, then the declaration block. A partial block never carries the marker.

Goldens proven, not blessed

Each changed golden carries a four-way hash proof. Removing SymbolNameLine and/or the complete-symbol signals reproduces every standalone golden exactly.

Benchmark harness facts

  • The paid path is run_cc_one.sh --execution-manifest → cc_attempt.py, which runs Claude Code with --dangerously-skip-permissions --safe-mode and identical disallowed tools in both arms. It is not a sandbox (hermetic: false).
  • The model is an unpinned alias (sonnet) with no allowlist and no reasoning-effort setting.
  • Tasks are SWE-bench Multilingual only. The frozen gate sets overlap the earlier rep30/rep100 lists; gate_10 is fine for a mechanics pilot but not for confirmation.
  • The pilot driver runs adjacent pairs serially, with a local admission threshold. Cancellation is cooperative only and cannot guarantee reaping a paid process if its parent hangs. The ledger fsync is untested.
  • Graph indexes for the 8 pilot tasks must be rebuilt with build dd76; 5 of gate_10 have old indexes, 5 have none.

Corrections made along the way

Logged so you can judge how much to trust the rest.

  • I said tests had passed before reading every shard (shard 0, and #302's code-order test). Both were wrong; corrected.
  • I said the no-tool baseline "would be contaminated" from a reviewer's guess. The harness already runs --safe-mode; retracted.
  • I called the finding-dismiss 404 a platform limit. It is a stale local CLI from 19 Aug that decodes empty review ids.
  • I miscounted 7 failing tests (it was 6), and edited a branch after Codex had frozen it for a test run (disclosed; the run stayed valid).
  • A docs agent said asyncRewake was undocumented. Checking the live docs page showed it is documented.

Decisions waiting on you, then open technical questions, then the rules every benchmark claim follows. Each decision lists the options and our recommendation.

Decisions for you

D1 · launch
Approve the launch candidate and stack?
Approve #315 (and #305 most urgently), or review per component PR.
Recommend: approve #305 now, since it fixes a real infinite hang. Then review #315, which needs a human or a longer automated review because the 15-min agent review timed out.
D2 · spend
Spending cap for the paid pilot?
A dollar figure, ideally on a dedicated API key with its own limit.
Recommend: a dedicated key with a hard provider limit. The runner can only stop before launching the next task; a single task can overshoot.
D3 · pilot
Small pilot (Option S) or phase-aware driver (Option L)?
S: the existing runner, one task pair at a time, graded once at the end. L: a canary hold, attested continuation and a new grading seam.
Recommend: S for the 8-pair mechanics pilot. Build L only if a confirmatory run follows.
D4 · metric
Primary measure: provider cost or token volume?
Cost (cache reads were 49% of cost earlier), or a raw token count, which can move opposite to cost.
Recommend: cost as primary, with every token component reported beside it, plus wall-clock time and turns.
D5 · estimand
Count every assigned task, or only tasks both arms solved?
Counting only successes can fake savings if one arm fails more on hard tasks.
Recommend: add an all-tasks measure beside the both-solved one. This changes an established project rule, so it is your call.
D6 · model
Which model, pinned how?
The runner defaults to the bare alias sonnet and has no effort flag.
Recommend: a dated model id in the run manifest; record the Claude Code version; no effort flag unless added as a reviewed change.
D7 · safety
Accept running the benchmark with permissions off?
The harness runs Claude Code with --dangerously-skip-permissions in a non-sandboxed runner.
Recommend: run it in a disposable VM or container for paid cells, not on your laptop.
D8 · cleanup
Update the local entire CLI and dismiss the two refuted findings?
Your binary is from 19 Aug; the current CLI dismisses correctly.
Recommend: rebuild from cli main, then dismiss the HIGH findings on #312 and #313. Public rebuttals are already posted.
D9 · product
Cap the warm preindex path?
Reusing a preindex is 4–5× slower and changes output, because it bypasses the file cap.
Recommend: yes. Fix it so default users get the fast path; studies 3–6 measured the warm path.
D10 · scope
Close #300 (semantic channel)?
Study 3 found no gain at equal budget.
Recommend: close it. Both agents agree.

Open technical questions

AreaQuestionWhere it stands
Pilot driverHow does a run continue past the canary pairs without a hidden resume feature?Out of scope. The driver stops at the canary and says so.
Pilot driverHow do we grade only the canary pairs without shipping empty patches for unrun tasks?No grading-subset seam exists yet; Option S grades all 8 at the end instead.
Pilot driverCan an abort guarantee the paid Claude process dies?Only with a child-side process-group file (Option A), which is unverified design. Option S is cooperative only.
Study 6Why did cases 26 and 184 show the header but not the declaration?Unexplained (seed or compaction stage). Case 156 was a real bug, fixed in #316.
Go routesEmbedded *http.Client, type aliases, wide switch fan-out of 17+ branches, closures nested 16+ deepKnown precision and recall limits, documented, not fixed
DatasetA clean confirmatory task set10 historical exclusion lists are lost, and the rep50/HOLD50/REP30F lists live only on VMs or in GCS.
AccuracyRoute evidence: guessed fallback vs proven registrationShould be marked separately before any public accuracy claim.

Rules every benchmark claim follows

Fairness

Ask of every instruction: would it help an arm with no tool? If yes, both arms get it or neither does. The VERIFY hint is suppressed in both arms.

Gate before scoring

Validity gates run before any scores are read. A pair counts only when both arms succeed with a non-empty patch, and pairs are dropped symmetrically.

Power from instances

Add tasks; never replicate one. Run-to-run noise was about 87% of paired variance. Always report a bootstrap CI and the median.

Audit the harness first

Every withdrawn headline here died of a harness bug: the token source field, asymmetric clamps, a shared cache, load pressure. Check the harness before blaming the tool.

No early reporting

Paired deltas have shrunk or flipped as n grew (+2.00 became −0.39). Results are reported only at full sample.

Claims stay scoped

Study wins are retrieval-only and configuration-specific. "Beats grep" always carries the caveat that it is a Go-shaped frozen policy.

I've sorted all 77 study-6 cases where the newest build missed the target by cause. I re-checked the counts against the per-case table.

- **Most misses are ranking, not display (66 of 77).**
  - In 13 the right file never reached the top 10.
  - In 51 the right file was found but a different symbol in it ranked instead of the target.
  - In 2 the target was nested inside another symbol.
- **10 of 77 are display bugs: the target was found but its declaration line wasn't printed.**
  - In 4, the target's section was merged with neighbouring code and the declaration was dropped from the output.
  - In 4, the declaration fell inside lines that merging pulled in, and it was never recorded at all.
  - In 2 (cases 26 and 184, previously unexplained), the target got its own result row, but the row showed only 2 lines and the declaration wasn't among them. Raising the byte budget a thousandfold doesn't change this, so it's a display bug, not a space limit.
- **1 is the annotation bug already fixed in PR #316.** That fix isn't in #315 yet.
- **Nothing was cut for space, and the scoring wasn't too strict anywhere:** in all 77 the declaration text appears nowhere in the output.

All of this is diagnosis after the fact. Study 6's result doesn't change, and I'm not claiming any new accuracy number.

**What I've proposed to Codex**, who controls the Go code, so the order is Codex's call:
- One small display PR, after #316 goes in, that prints the declaration line for found targets. That could recover up to 10 of these misses, but that's an upper bound and unverified.
- Tests built from made-up cases shaped like these, not the study cases themselves, so we don't tune to the scoring set.
- Any re-measurement on a fresh, preregistered task set.

The 66 ranking misses are the bigger, harder piece of work.

The paid-pilot script is frozen at its final version (commit `e72140e`) and handed to Codex. Codex is running its tests once on a separate, untouched copy. I re-ran the 57 tests myself and they pass.

**What the script now does:** a run that didn't complete may continue only if the validator's reason is exactly "never sealed" (`seal_missing`). Any other reason stops the pilot, including reasons added in future versions. The money already spent stays counted, and the paired run in the other arm is not launched. A test confirms that a real failed run does produce "never sealed", so the rule isn't trivially satisfied.

**The one-off test failure now has a likely cause.** It's a bug in the fake launcher the tests use, not in the script itself.
- When the stop signal arrived while a heartbeat file was being closed, the fake launcher's exit was swallowed and it kept running. After 10 seconds the script force-killed it, as designed.
- The builder fixed the fake launcher. The real cancellation code and the 10-second grace period are unchanged.
- The proof comes from a reproduction run whose temporary folder has since been deleted. I copied its error output out of the builder's log into a file and told Codex where it is.
- It isn't proof for the very first failure, whose files were also deleted, though that one failed in exactly the same way.
- The builder also re-ran the test far more times than Codex had asked. I disclosed that.

**Two items for the PR description:**
- If a test times out rather than fails a check, the new failure details aren't captured; the test's description claims more than it delivers.
- The rule relies on the launcher only ever writing the "sealed" file on success.

**Accuracy follow-up:**
- Codex agreed to the small fix that shows the declaration on 2-line result rows (cases 26 and 184), to be built with a test that fails first.
- The other display behaviour, where declarations get dropped from merged sections, is deliberate and already tested. Changing it trades output size against quality, so that one is your call.
- PR #316 now passes all CI and only needs your approval.

Nothing paid has run and nothing has been pushed. Approving #305, setting a spending cap and reviewing #315 are still waiting on you.

The analysis of why the graph ranked the wrong code first in study 6 is done, and it turned up a gap in the launch candidate.

**The gap, which I checked myself:** PR #291 isn't in #315. That's the fix that computes word rarity across the whole repo instead of a sample of files. **Why the target got outranked (66 misses):** this split comes from a Python stand-in for the scoring code that agrees with the real build about 79% of the time. Treat it as a strong lead, not proof.
- **9 misses can't be fixed by tuning.** The query shares almost no words with the target, so only meaning-based search could find them.

  - Removing the bonus recovered 6 misses and lost no hits in the stand-in.
  - The bonus was added for a different style of query, so changing it needs a fresh test set first.
- **Ruled out:** short functions, test files, methods, and whether the file was ever considered. Each was just as common among the correct results, so none explains the misses.

**Proposed order to Codex:**
1. Decide whether #291 belongs in #315.
2. Fix the crowding, tested on made-up cases first.
3. Touch the name bonus only with a fresh test set on repos we haven't tuned on.

content.text:
The study 7 plan is drafted, and I've sent it to Codex to try to find holes in it. Nothing has run.

- **Tests the normal setup:** it runs the search exactly as a user gets it by default, with no saved index. So it needs no index builds and avoids the cache problem study 6 had, but its numbers can't be compared with studies 5 and 6.
- **Only search time changes:** both fixes touch only the code that runs at search time, so all versions read the same parsed code.
- **Six versions of the tool:**
  - the current candidate;
  - each crowding fix alone, and both together;
  - two versions of the weaker name bonus.
- **720 targets on 12 fresh repos:** three repos each in Go, Python, Java and TypeScript.
  - 480 use plain-English queries written from the code's comments with the function name hidden, by an agent that isn't told what's being tested.
  - 240 use function names.
- **Passing rules:** a fix "passes" only if it finds the target more often, doesn't lose too many cases, and the cause it targets actually goes down. A score gain without that gets flagged as noise.
- **Size, honestly:**
  - The name-bonus question has about an 80% chance of detecting an effect the size the earlier stand-in suggested, and less if the effect is smaller.
  - The crowding question has only about a 55% chance. The fix probably didn't help the example cases either, so "no effect shown" is the likely result there.
- **Cost:** no model calls and about 19,500 searches, roughly 5.5–11 hours on one core. A smaller version takes 3–6 hours.
- **Side findings:**
  - A code comment wrongly says the name bonus is weighted by word rarity; the code itself says it deliberately isn't.
  - The name-bonus variants would probably break an existing calibration test, so even a pass would be evidence, not a ready-to-merge change.

Codex's adversarial review of PREREG-DRAFT.md (sha a94923a9...) says NOT READY TO FREEZE. Revise the PAPER ONLY, same rules as before: no runs, builds, fetches, dummies, graph, go or network. Write PREREG-DRAFT-v2.md beside v1, plus a REVIEW-RESPONSE.md that maps each point to its fix. RESOLVE decisions; do not add arms or scale. Caveman-ultra report when done.

Blockers:
1. JSON at 4096 is NOT the agent-4096 identity by design. cli/search.go:333-338 sets semantic MaxContextBytes=0 for agent; JSON keeps 4096. Agent output groups and fits separately (~1600/1706), and the budget shapes allocation and related merging before serialization. The real agent blocks define the measured payload. Any metadata join needs exact row identity plus rules for missing or ambiguous rows; headers can't recover signals or raw scores.
2. json100 changes retrieval: sem/search.go:2155-2179 (file bounds 96 at top-10 vs 256 at 100), :1136-1142 (progressive preselection), :5617 (distinct-file target 5 -> 50). Explicit max-indexed-files 96 disables progressive selection. Keep it exploratory only. Mechanisms need the actual top-10 pipeline stage; uncapped final JSON10 comes after the related merge and can't reconstruct the pre-displacement state or whether B fired. No instrumentation is approved, so the mechanism endpoints must be redesigned or downgraded accordingly.
3. Env policy: scrubbing ENTIRE_GRAPH* leaves EG_PRESEARCH, EG_SEARCH_SESSION and EG_MAX_SEARCHES (cli/env.go:27-35, 92-105). EG_PRESEARCH echoes a file before search (cli/search.go:193-197). Use a declared allowlist or a complete documented scrub, and bind the effective env in receipts without secret values.
4. GI symbol equality is only enumerator/target compatibility, not query completeness: the query fills OnlyFiles from selection (sem/search.go:1334-1371). Rename or restrict GI; keep preselection misses in the denominator. Partial-failure health must use the structured query fields, not the absence of a stderr warning.
5. The freeze order is circular. Use linked immutable freezes: a protocol freeze, then an artifact/run freeze. GB exempts BASE from parent==base; compare normalized buildinfo; give dummy builds an explicit timestamp exception.
6. Claim scope: Q2 is 480 targets, not 720. Split the Q1 and Q2 claims and name the population (generated queries, 12 selected repos). Pinned repos don't make pairs independent: McNemar and the power figures are a working model, not an exact design-proved inference. Decide cluster sensitivity, its decision role, and cross-family multiplicity before freezing.
7. The s1 guard L<=W+2 is not non-inferiority, and the added p>.10 is redundant (given the guard, p>=.25). Either call it a count guard honestly, or preregister an absolute loss margin with a confidence-bound rule.
8. Failure-conditioned mechanism sets shrink mechanically whenever there is a rescue, so label them mechanism-consistency diagnostics, not causal attribution. Define AB's BASE set as a union or intersection.

Also:
- Label the power tables as covering primary + LG(i) only (Codex reproduced every cell, size ~.0069), not the full acceptance rule.
- Correct the claims "no graph construction / no cache / every call physically cold": queries build selective snapshots, per-call content caches exist, and OS warmth is uncontrolled. The supportable claim is "no preparatory persistent index and no persistent worktree snapshot reuse".
- Calls: 17,766..22,086 plus dummies. json100 and GI are different cost classes. <=22 core-hours is an estimate, not a cap; require a separately authorized total stop budget.
- The symmetric ±1% byte gate also rejects a cheaper arm. Choose between equal ceiling, no payload increase, or equal realized bytes, and justify the choice.
- Restate scope: retrieval research only, which cannot establish end-to-end token or task savings.
Keep v1 unchanged.

content.text:
Codex reviewed the study 7 plan and says it isn't ready to lock in.

- **The two biggest problems:**
  - The planned way of measuring which result rows the agent sees isn't the same as what the agent actually sees. The two output formats lay out results differently within the size limit.
  - The deeper run I planned for checking causes actually changes which results get picked. So it can't show why a case was missed in the normal run.
- **Other fixes:** a full list of the environment settings that can change behaviour, clearer limits on what the results can claim, a fixed order for locking each part of the plan, honest labels on the statistics, and a separately approved total CPU budget.

The agent that drafted the plan is now writing a second version that fixes every point, plus a note matching each fix to its point. It's paper only: nothing runs, is built, or is downloaded.

GitHub CI on graphmark #96 now passes. #317 is still waiting on two platforms.

Still waiting on you:
1. A spending cap for the paid token-savings test.
2. Approvals for #305, #316, #317 and graphmark #96.
3. A review of #315.

  4. **Completeness.** GI renamed GC (enumerator/target compatibility, not query completeness).
     - Preselection misses stay in the denominator.
     - New gate GQ uses json0 structured fields: partial_failures (search.go:572); warnings and completeness.health reported.
     - Limits: ≤1% degraded per fixture per arm, and degraded file sets identical across arms.

content.text:
The second version of the study 7 plan is written and with Codex for another review. It's still paper only.

It addresses all 8 of Codex's objections:
- **What gets scored:** only the output the agent actually sees. A matching data dump of exactly the input behind that output replaces the old measurement.
- **The deeper diagnostic run:** it's now optional and kept separate, so a problem there can't invalidate the main results.
- **Causes:** these become consistency checks, not claims that a fix caused a gain.
- **Environment settings:** a fixed list, and nothing outside it is allowed.
- **Locking the plan:** two steps, first the method and then the inputs and budget.
- **What it can claim:**
  - The two questions are reported separately.
  - A fix only counts if its gain holds up when each of the 12 repos is dropped in turn, so one repo can't carry the result.
  - The check on name-style queries is honestly labelled a simple count, not a statistical guarantee.
- **Cost:** a hard CPU stop budget that you would set.
- **Output size:** a fix may make output smaller, but not more than 1% bigger.
- **Scope:** the plan opens by saying this is search-accuracy research only and can't prove token savings on real tasks.

Running it would still need Codex's approval and your go-ahead.

Still waiting on you:
1. A spending cap for the paid token-savings test.
2. Approvals for #305, #316, #317 and graphmark #96.
3. A review of #315.

=== session-length-is-the-mechanism

**The one relationship that survives every test.** Across 93 paired rep30/Opus+Haiku instances:

```
WINNERS n=63   messages 46.3 → 35.7 (−23.0%)   tokens −34.0%
LOSERS  n=30   messages 37.7 → 47.1 (+25.0%)   tokens +38.8%
corr(message-count delta, token delta) = 0.947
```

Cost ≈ messages × accumulated context, so every "phase regression" is downstream of session length. The `other` bucket hands back 13.06M tokens with *flat call counts* (cat/head/sed 701→709) — the calls are not extra, they are later.

**The decisive asymmetry: winners had LONGER baselines (46.3 msgs) than losers (37.7).** The tool wins when the control would have flailed and loses when the control was already efficient — on a short session there is nothing to delete and the payload can only add.

**Regression ledger (90 pairs, control 234M, tool 199M, actual −15.1%):** places where the tool spends MORE hand back **43.21M = 18.5% of control spend**. If no phase ever regressed: **−33.6%**. The whole gap to any target is give-backs, not missing savings.

**TEN payload-quality metrics have now failed to move tokens** — editability, line coverage, file coverage, confidence gap, covering-test presence, rank-1 correctness, and four earlier ones. Treat this as a law, not a hypothesis to keep testing. Notably:
- LINE coverage does NOT discriminate winners from losers: 24.7% vs 26.8%, gap points the WRONG way, Fisher p=0.83, r=+0.004, MH OR=0.969, robust across 7 tolerance settings. The prior "39pt gap" claim traces to a 4-loser Haiku slice.
- Rank-1 correctness: gold at rank 1 saving 10.9% (n=39) vs wrong file saving 9.1% (n=43) — a 1.8pt gap inside a 33.9pt noise floor.
- Five of six cells share BYTE-IDENTICAL payloads (FILE 76.7% / LINE 23.3%) while win-rate spans 63–80% and mean delta spans −23.8% to +10.3%. A constant cannot explain a variable.

**Also measured:** the agent never invokes the graph interactively (0 calls in 39 sessions); native MCP registration does not change this (tools arrive as `deferred_tools_delta`, `ToolSearch` never called). Environment archaeology is symmetric (49 vs 49 Bash calls). The harness injects ONLY rank 1 (`pf_minimal` regexes `^1\.`), discarding a payload that contains gold in top-3 67% of the time to assert a single line correct 47% of the time — a real defect, but measurably NOT a token lever.

Related: [[rep30-two-clean-cells-verdict]], [[payload-metrics-graveyard]], [[benchmark-arm-fairness-bugs]].
=== agentic-token-saving-is-the-clamp

Controlled experiment in graphmark/agentic-swebench (configs P2 vs P3, `.p2_haiku` 30 instances, haiku, all three arms re-run fresh in both cells). The two cells are identical — same `PROMPT_FAMILY=thorough`, same md5-identical `shared_block` on all arms, same instances, same build (`integ/measure-2026-07-28 @0af923e`), same eg k10 / cmm 7-3 wrapper params, same 50-turn cap — **except** that in P2 eg's arm block carried six frugality-clamp phrases the other arms did not, and in P3 every arm block is a pure capability description (clamp count verified 0/0/0 in the rendered prompts).

| cell | eg turns vs baseline | eg vs baseline usd | eg vs cmm usd |
|---|---|---|---|
| P2 (clamp on eg only) | 31.03 vs 40.47 | **−25.8%** | −33.9% |
| P3 (no clamp anywhere) | 38.60 vs 39.57 | **−0.9%** | **+6.8%** |

**The token saving is the frugality instruction, not the code graph.** Remove it and the advantage collapses to noise and eg loses to cmm.

**Why it matters:** every published eg-vs-baseline token headline (−54.9%, −45.8%, −32.3%/−31.6%) was measured with eg under a clamp its comparator lacked. The clamp also costs accuracy (published round −19 resolves; P2 here −4, two of them eg stopping early, one an empty patch at 7 turns). **Structural reason it can't be fixed by configuration:** ~39 of 39.6 turns are not locate. A locate accelerator cannot shorten the fix/verify loop, which is where the cost is. === graph-swebench-verdict

Measured (not predicted) verdict of the entire-graph agentic-swebench benchmark (haiku, 30-task pilot, SWE-bench Multilingual), `~/Documents/Coding/brain-swebench`. Settles the long "make the graph win >20% tokens AND significantly-more accuracy" goal.

**Tokens — graph WINS (lean graph = def/callers/callees):** vs a whole-file-naive baseline (faithful mini-swe-agent, = Thomas's 40% setup): **−19% $cost, −23% total tokens, −12.4% real tokens.** The measurement was the issue (user's "99.99% harness" point): an agent-picks-its-own-reads naive proxy gave only −11% (too smart); forcing whole-file `cat` (mini-swe-agent's actual behavior) gives −23%. Smart Claude Code baseline understates the graph (−1%). Per-lookup deterministic = −93%.

**Accuracy — ~0, noise-band, NOT movable via the graph:** two full 30-runs gave **+1 and −3** (baseline 15→t16; baseline 17→t14). haiku per-task variance is ±100%, so ±3/30 is noise. The graph helps you FIND code, not WRITE fixes — solve-rate is coding-ability-bound. Proven structurally AND empirically.

**Last-resort graph enrichment BACKFIRED (measured):** added `tests <sym>` (covering tests + source) / `impls <sym>` queries + a "read the covering tests before editing" prompt. Result: tokens −23%→−4% (agent over-reads test bodies) AND accuracy −3 (overfits to shown tests → regressions on hidden tests). **Reverted** the prompt push; kept `tests`/`impls` as optional `graph-query` commands (they're correct, just not routine). The lean graph was already the better tool.

**Budget-regime test (40-turn cap, cheap-deployment) ALSO failed both:** accuracy baseline 10 → treated 9 (−1, noise); tokens +2.1% (treated worse — at a tight cap both arms truncate before the graph's read-avoidance accrues, and gq query overhead shows). So the token win is regime-specific: it needs a FULL session + naive baseline; under a budget or with enrichment it evaporates.

**Brief lever (round-trip collapse) — built, measured, net-negative for haiku, REVERTED (injection off; `gq brief` kept as a tool):** auto-injecting a task-scoped packet (top issue-relevant symbols + source, ranked) up front to skip iterative navigation. brief-6: AGG real **+19.6%** (worse). Two failure modes: (1) string-match ranking is noisy (fmt got printf *headers*, nushell/redis matched generic words) — precise text→code needs embeddings, i.e. the BRAIN's vector search; `SIMILAR_TO` edges are code→code, don't help text→code; (2) even a CORRECT brief doesn't stop haiku exploring on a complex fix (fmt: right brief, still gq=13 / 17→71 turns). It only won when the brief was precise AND the fix simple: **druid −42%, immutable −30%** — proof the mechanism CAN clear −40%, gated on brief precision + agent compliance.

**Architecture conclusion (vindicates graph+brain):** graph-ALONE tops out at −23% (lean); pushing to −40% needs **precise briefs = the brain's semantic (vector) ranking on top of the graph** (druid proves −42% with a precise brief) AND a compliant agent. So Thomas's 40% "fix completely," if it's a context/brief result, is a graph+brain number, not graph-alone. The graph is the structural substrate; the brain supplies text→code relevance.

**v2 precise brief (file:line + code-fence + dep-exclusion ranking) — regressed at N=30 on BOTH axes:** looked great on a 6-task pick (real −24%, redis −52%/nushell −41%) but that sample was winner-biased. Full N=30: **real −8.7% / cost −14.5% / total −18.9% — WORSE than lean on every metric** (injection cache-read overhead + complex-fix draggers). Accuracy **+0/30** (baseline 15 → treated 15; 2 wins druid/gson ± 2 regressions fmt/hugo = variance). So accuracy is now flat across **6 configs** (100t +1/−3, enriched −3, budget −1, sonnet −1, v2-brief +0) — even a PRECISE brief that lands the agent on the exact code (gq=0) doesn't lift resolved%, because finding≠fixing. Same small-sample-optimism → N=30-regression pattern as every enrichment. **Lean graph (−19% cost / −23% total, accuracy-flat) is the robust ceiling; additions consistently make it worse.** Canonical 30-task baseline frozen at `results/haiku_baseline_canonical` (15/30 resolved) so treated-only experiments stop re-running it. BRIEF_INJECT gated OFF by default.

**Harness-suppression correction (2026-07-19) — accuracy WAS being under-measured, then hit a real wall at 60%:** the flat-accuracy runs used a crippled harness (default effort, one-shot "just stop", no verify). Deep audit found it: haiku near-misses (28/30 patches in the SAME file as gold — navigates right, fails on a detail/completeness). Fixing the harness climbs it, clean pass@1: naive one-shot 15/30 (50%) → smart+VERIFY(TDD iteration) 16/30 (53%) → smart+graph+VERIFY+effort=high 18/30 (60%) → effort=max 18/30 (60%, PLATEAU, two independent clean runs agree). So the harness was suppressing ~10pt (real, recovered) and haiku now beats its published Multilingual (~50%). **But 60% is the honest pass@1 ceiling; Sonnet 5 = 78.3% pass@1 is +18pt beyond it — a model-tier wall.** IMPORTANT integrity note: re-running ONLY the failures and keeping passes gave a spurious "70%" — that's pass@k / eval-selection, NOT pass@1; refused to report it. Opus (84.4%) is the only honest path >78.3%. New harness levers added: `VERIFY` (TDD iteration prompt) + `CC_EFFORT` (extended-thinking) in run_cc_one.sh, `gq similar`/`brief` in graph-query.

**Smart-baseline accuracy test (the "right" accuracy comparison) — ALSO flat:** hypothesis: 6 flat configs all used a whole-file-naive baseline that reads EVERYTHING → zero accuracy headroom (graph can't help you find code you already read); a SELECTIVE (Read/Grep) baseline can miss scattered code → graph's precise refs could rescue incomplete fixes. Tested smart baseline vs smart+graph on 8 baseline-failed tasks: **baseline 1/8, treated 1/8 = +0** (ripgrep won, bat regressed). So accuracy is flat against BOTH baseline types — the failures aren't from missing code (grep finds it), they're from writing the wrong fix (coding). **7 accuracy configs total, all ~0.** finding≠fixing is structural, not a baseline artifact.

**How it was reached without cheating:** 3 models × 2 baselines × 5 harness levers × median-of-3 × per-lookup × enrichment × budget × brief-v1/v2 × smart-baseline-accuracy. Accuracy measured ~0 in **7 configs** (100t +1/−3, enriched −3, budget −1, sonnet −1, v2-brief +0, smart-baseline +0). Refused to inflate the baseline beyond faithful-mini-swe-agent, cherry-pick runs, or tune-to-target. See [[cost-analytics-state]], [[orchestrator-architecture]].

**OPUS head-to-head (2026-07-19, 15 tasks sampled evenly from the OFFICIAL 300, not the pilot; 13 evaluated — redis/tokio docker images won't build locally):** baseline(no graph) 11/13 = **85%**, treated(+graph) 10/13 = **77%**, graph accuracy Δ **−1** (0 graph wins, 1 regression rubocop = noise). Tokens: graph **−5.4% real / −6.2% cost** (smaller than haiku-naive −23% because opus navigates efficiently in smart mode). So the pattern holds on a FRONTIER model too: **graph = token/navigation win, accuracy-neutral.** Opus baseline 85% already clears its published 84.4% + Sonnet 5's 78.3% on its own — it's a strong coder; the graph just makes it ~5-6% cheaper at equal accuracy. NOTE on eval infra: a random 300-sample needs docker images BUILT locally (`--namespace none`); default pulls from swebench dockerhub → 404 for unpublished tasks; and Docker Desktop VM disk fills fast (prune between builds). The 300-sampled task file is `opus15_tasks.json`; harness now reads `TASKS_FILE` env.

=== stats-savings-was-inflated

`entire graph stats` credited each graph locate call with "the ONE whole-file read it
replaced", priced at the on-disk size of the top-hit file (falling back to the repo's median
tracked-file size). **Both inputs were guesses.** On identical data: old model **82.9M
tokens saved**, new model **~46k** — roughly **1800x** inflated.

**The replacement (PR #213) calibrates per session, from the transcript already parsed:**
```
graph cost/call       = GraphReturnedBytes       / graph locate calls
exploration cost/call = ExplorationReturnedBytes / exploration calls
saving/substitution   = max(0, exploration cost/call − graph cost/call)
```
Both inputs measured, same repo, same task. The only assumption left is 1:1 substitution,
and this repo measured that at **0.980 calls displaced per call**
([[graph-is-a-1to1-substitute]]) — so it is empirically grounded, not invented.

**The sanity check that validates it:** per-session deltas came out 4 positive / 4 negative,
**mean negative** — consistent with our own paired A/B ([[the-fair-number-is-2-5-percent]]:
COST +2.49%, CI [−6.83, +11.18], median negative, graph output *larger* per call). The old
model contradicted our own benchmark by three orders of magnitude. **A savings number that
disagrees with the paired benchmark is wrong, not impressive.**

**A real bug found underneath it:** 215 `tool_use` ids and 168 usage-bearing `message.id`s
appear in more than one transcript *of the same session* — Claude Code replays a forked
subagent's history — and both copies were billed. Measured over 3,316 files, zero
=== cost-decomposition-closes-25pct

2026-08-11. Every scorer this campaign used summed input+output+cacheRead+cacheCreation with EQUAL
weight, i.e. token COUNT. Scoring `total_cost_usd` (recorded in every `cc_out.json`, previously used
only as a gate) makes the number **worse, not better**:

```
REP30F n=28   tokens +7.16%    COST +5.21%  CI [-7.02,+16.82]  median +4.92%  wins 14/28
ER12   n=11   tokens +2.00%    COST +3.03%
  per class:  cacheRead +7.40%   output +4.64%   cacheCreation +0.13%   input -1.62%
```

Prices solved by least squares on 83 sessions, **residual 0.0%**, and the ratios match Opus exactly
(output/cacheRead = 50.0 vs 75/1.50; cacheCreation/cacheRead = 12.5 vs 18.75/1.50):

```
class            tokens     tok %      cost     COST %
cacheRead   279,527,336    95.80%   $139.83    48.85%
output        3,769,817     1.29%    $94.27    32.93%   <- 1.3% of tokens, a THIRD of cost
cacheCreation 8,325,233     2.85%    $51.96    18.15%
input           162,703     0.06%     $0.19     0.07%
```

**To reach 25% COST saving, holding the others at today's figures:** cacheRead alone must save
**48.0%**, output alone **64.9%**, cacheCreation alone 109.4% (impossible), or all three **25% each**.
Today: 7.40 / 4.64 / 0.13. Every component is 5-15x short.
=== the-number-is-8-6-percent

Measured 2026-08-10. Same 50 instances (`rep50x.json`), same machine, same day, three runs. Both
interventions were proven inert by their own mechanism endpoints, so all three effectively measure one
configuration:

```
REP50X    +2.89%   (n=48)   pre-registered, criteria declared in advance
CS50     +12.84%   (n=47)   call sites v1, mechanism refuted
CS50B     +9.94%   (n=45)   call sites v2, mechanism refuted
mean      +8.56%   sd 4.18pt   range 9.95pt
```

**Quote ~+8.6%.** It converges from three independent aggregations: 3-run mean +8.56%, pooling
REP50X+CS50 as pairs +8.11%, lifetime total +9.52%.

**Cell-level noise is ~4–5pt sd / ~10pt range at n≈48.** +16.10%, +12.84%, +9.94% and +2.89% are the
same measurement wearing different hats. Never quote a single 50-cell without its interval.

The two metrics disagree and answer different questions: token-weighted **pooled** = +8–9% (determines
the bill); **per-instance mean** = −2.92%, CI [−14.6, +7.7] (weights every task equally; savings live
in the tail). For "what does this save on a workload," pooled is the right one.

**Lifetime: 68,639,272 tokens saved, +9.52%, $1,421 of measurement.**

Codex reviewed the second version of the study 7 plan. The big problems from the first review are fixed, but it isn't ready to lock in yet. Codex asked for eight small corrections to the document:
- **Version check:** every test build must carry the exact source version it claims to be.
- **Evidence protection:** results from the main phases get locked before the optional diagnostic phase starts, so stopping early can't erase them.
- **CPU limit wording:** describe it honestly. It stops new work from starting rather than capping usage live.
- **Missing data:** a missing or broken data dump counts as "invalid", never as a miss.
- **Combined error rate:** state it as "at most 10%" across the two questions, rather than an exact figure.

16	`entire graph` is a local, offline code-intelligence plugin for the Entire CLI.

224	**Why it exists:** ranking and every relation verb need a structural model of the code: where each symbol starts and ends, what its name line is, and what it calls, extends, uses and serves.
225	
226	### 3.1 Parser and languages
227	
228	- **Parser.** Tree-sitter, through `github.com/smacker/go-tree-sitter` (`go.mod`; `provider.go:parserVersions:227`).
229	  - Upstream grammars are imported in `sem/parser.go:14-49`: bash, C, C++, CUE, Elixir, Go, HCL, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, Lua, OCaml, PHP, Protobuf, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Swift, TypeScript/TSX, YAML.
230	  - Vendored grammars live in `internal/sem/grammars/`: Clojure, C#, Dart, Erlang, F#, Haskell, Julia, Objective-C, Perl, R, Zig. SQL is in `internal/sem/pgsql` and zsh in `internal/sem/zsh`.
231	  - Groovy has no grammar and uses a structural scanner (`sem/groovy.go`).
232	- **Semantic vs inventory-only.**
233	  - A language is semantic if it is not marked `inventoryOnly` and either has a grammar or is SQL or Groovy (`provider.go:supportsSemanticExtraction:722`).
234	  - The inventory tier is `inventoryLanguageExtensions` (`sem/inventory_languages.go:6`). Its definition: languages "recognized deterministically and emit stable document symbols, but they do not claim rich language-aware relation extraction."
235	  - `docs/language-support.md` counts 185 names: 36 semantic and 149 inventory-only. It warns that inventory coverage "must not be counted as semantic-resolution parity".
236	  - Each snapshot header carries per-language tiers (`SnapshotHeader.LanguageTiers`, `provider.go:248`).
237	- **Relation vocabulary.** 30 types (`provider.go:relationTypes:68`):
238	  - Structure and calls: DEFINES, CONTAINS, IMPORTS, CALLS, CONSTRUCTS, ASYNC_CALLS.
239	  - Inheritance: EXTENDS, INHERITS, IMPLEMENTS, OVERRIDES.
240	  - Types and fields: USES_TYPE, PARAM_TYPE, RETURNS_TYPE, READS_FIELD, WRITES_FIELD, ACCESSES.
241	  - Services and events: HANDLES_ROUTE, HANDLES_GRPC, HANDLES_GRAPHQL, HANDLES_TRPC, HTTP_CALLS, EMITS, LISTENS_ON, HANDLES_TOOL.
242	  - Config and tests: CONFIGURES, RESOURCE_DEPENDS_ON, TESTS.
243	  - Inferred: SIMILAR_TO, DATA_FLOWS, FILE_CHANGES_WITH.
244	- **Which languages get which relations** (`provider.go:ooRelationSupport:105`):
245	
246	  | Language(s) | Relations beyond the structural set |
247	  |---|---|
248	  | Java, TypeScript, C#, Rust | Full object-oriented set |
249	  | Go | USES_TYPE, PARAM_TYPE, RETURNS_TYPE, READS_FIELD, WRITES_FIELD, ACCESSES, ASYNC_CALLS, DATA_FLOWS. No EXTENDS or IMPLEMENTS |
250	  | Ruby | INHERITS, USES_TYPE, DATA_FLOWS only; the comment says header inheritance "is not parsed yet" |
251	  | Elixir, Lua, Perl, R, SQL | DATA_FLOWS only |
252	  | HCL, YAML, Dockerfile, Kustomize | CONFIGURES, RESOURCE_DEPENDS_ON |
253	  | GraphQL | HANDLES_GRAPHQL |
254	  | Protobuf | HANDLES_GRPC |
255	
256	  The comments are candid about precision:
257	  - Data flow "is regex-driven over a callable's body".
258	  - USES_TYPE resolves "against every type symbol in the repository by short name", so it can credit a foreign type in a polyglot repository (`provider.go:~142-152`).
259	  - On Zig: "An over-declared relation fails an agent the same way an under-declared one does."
260	
261	### 3.2 What the index stores
262	
263	- **Schema constants.** `SchemaVersion="1.3"`, `StableSymbolIDVersion="compound-v1"`, `IdentityRevision="3"` (`provider.go:42-54`).
264	- **`SymbolRecord`** (`provider.go:335`).
265	  - Public fields: id, kind, name, qualified_name, file_path, start and end line, signature, body_hash, language, container_id, and aliases. Aliases are names bound through registration tables such as `commands/<name>.json`.
266	  - Private parse metadata, kept out of the frozen schema: Local (closures), exact tree-sitter byte range, `nameLine`, bodyless (TypeScript overloads), C++ owners, parameter names, and parameter and return type text.
267	- **`RelationRecord`** (`provider.go:400`): from, to, type, confidence, reason, relation_scope, resolution, target_kind, evidence (`Evidence:421`: kind, file, lines, detail), warning_codes, evidence_dropped.
268	- **`SnapshotHeader`** (`provider.go:237`): repo_key, commit, tree, languages and tiers, capabilities, profile and limits, relation set, skipped families, warnings, partial_failures, stats, and completeness (per-language files and symbols, per-relation counts, health).
269	- **NameLine** (`sem/declaration_name_line.go`, header ~9-33). StartLine is often a decorator or annotation, and earlier text scanning misread such lines; *"The parser already knows the answer."* The name line is chosen in this order:
270	  1. the grammar's `name` or `property` field;
271	  2. for C-family declarations, the identifier the declarator binds;
272	  3. the first identifier spelled like the name, outside comments and literals and before the body.
273	
274	  The search is bounded by `nameLineVisitBudget=4096`. Regex-fallback extractors leave it at 0 and consumers fall back to the text heuristic. Symbols restored from a compact snapshot have no name line.
275	- **Build pipeline** (`provider.go:StreamSnapshot:1238`). The doc comment: *"Phase 1 lists the files, then parses each one and emits its file and symbol records immediately … Phase 2 resolves relations against those indexes."* The phases are Inventory → Parse → Relations → Finalize.
276	  - Relations come from `forEachRelation:4740`. It uses structural edges, a global short-name index (so shallow resolution can still reach cross-file targets) and a cross-file container index (e.g. a Go receiver in another file).
277	  - FILE_CHANGES_WITH comes from Git history (§5.2), SIMILAR_TO from `sem/similarity.go:160`, and TESTS from `provider.go:12359`.
278	- **Parallel but deterministic** (`sem/provider_parallel.go:runProviderFilePipeline:290`). Workers are bounded by GOMAXPROCS and results are reduced in exact index order. The comment: *"the work is parallel and the output is not … worker timing cannot reach the emitted bytes."*
279	- **Limits.**
280	  - Files over 4 MiB keep their file record and get a partial failure, with no symbols (`defaultMaxParseBytes`, `provider.go:~56`).
281	  - At most 200,000 source files (`ENTIRE_GRAPH_MAX_FILES`). Truncation emits `W_FILE_LIMIT` and is "never silent" (`provider.go:57-66, resolveMaxSourceFiles:13954, capSourceFiles:13976`).
282	
283	### 3.3 Go HTTP route extraction
284	
285	**Why it exists:** "which handler serves `/api/v1/foo`" is a common agent question, and the answer usually sits behind router groups and prefixes that grep cannot compose.
286	
287	- **Entry point.** `sem/go_route_registrations.go:goRouteRegistrationsDetailed:74`, called from `provider.go:goHTTPRouteRelations` (~24847).
288	- **Real calls only.** Routes *"are read from real call expressions only … Route-like text inside comments and string literals is never a call expression"* (`go_route_registrations.go:13-21`).
289	  - A regex gate (`goRouteCallHintRe:62`) skips files with nothing route-like.
290	  - Prefix calls are masked so the fallback scan cannot re-emit them (`goRoutePrefixHintRe:66`).
291	- **Frameworks:** gin, echo, fiber, gorilla/mux, chi, net/http, httprouter.
292	- **Prefix joining** follows each framework's own rules (`goRouteJoin`, ~185):
293	  - gin uses `path.Join` but keeps a trailing slash;
294	  - echo concatenates;
295	  - fiber trims the prefix's trailing slash and adds a leading one;
296	  - mux trims the parent's trailing slash.
297	
298	  Relative or empty paths are accepted only for gin, echo and fiber (`goRouteLiteral`, ~165).
299	- **Receiver resolver** (`sem/go_route_binding.go`, design comment lines 12-75). The old per-name fixed point *"failed to terminate (rebound names, naming cycles)"*. The new resolver *"walks the syntax tree once, in statement order, and records the prefix state of every identifier at its use site."* Each receiver is in one of three states:
300	  - **untracked**: a parameter of a type it cannot see; treated as the root router.
301	  - **known**: bound to a Group call with a static prefix.
302	  - **unknown**: the binding cannot be trusted.
303	
304	  A receiver becomes unknown on writes inside branches, loops or closures, on an address-of, when the function uses goto, on field or index receivers, on an escaping mount, under StripPrefix, or when the step budget runs out.
305	- **Fail-closed rules.**
306	  - `goRouteCandidateRoute` (~133) returns false whenever the receiver, mount origin or literal is undetermined: *"emitting the bare path, or another binding's prefix, would invent a route."*
307	  - The step budget is `1<<21` plus 64 per byte, and composed prefixes are capped at 2048 bytes (`go_route_binding.go:409-423`).
308	  - Exhausting the budget panics with `goRouteBudgetExceeded`. The panic is recovered and that file's group-capable routes are omitted (~302-307).
309	  - A named handler that is not a symbol in the file is attributed to the enclosing symbol, *"never dropped to the bare path"* (`provider.go:~24879`).
310	  - Gin `Group("v1")` without a leading slash is omitted, not guessed.
311	
312	### 3.4 The cache
313	
314	- **Location** (`cli/env.go:resolveCacheDir:~59`). Tried in order: `--cache-dir`, then `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`, then `os.UserCacheDir()/entire-graph` (`~/Library/Caches/entire-graph` on macOS).
315	  - It is one global directory, *"namespaced by product, not by repository: the cache is keyed on the git tree hash"* (`env.go:38-56`; ADR 0002).
316	- **Two cache families:**
317	  - **Search snapshot** `search-snapshot-v18-3` (`sem/search_cache.go:37`), stored at `<dir>/search/<ver>/<sha256>.json.gz`. Derived selective entries nest under the complete entry's key directory, with a `.generation.json.gz` marker (`cache_entry.go:newDerivedCacheEntry`).
318	  - **Provider records** `provider-records-v11-3` (`sem/records_cache.go`), the raw NDJSON for `snapshot`, `symbols` and `edges`.
319	- **Key** (`search_cache.go:searchSnapshotKeyForSchema:981`). SHA-256 over length-prefixed fields (`cache_key.go:writeCacheKeyField`). The fields:
320	  - cache version and schema version;
321	  - absolute repository path and repo key;
322	  - provider version and **HEAD tree** (the tree, not the commit);
323	  - profile, max-parse-bytes and the *resolved* max-files (a capped build once served 28 symbols instead of 5,740);
324	  - the sorted only-files list;
325	  - the built-in secret-rules digest;
326	  - the captured ignore policy.
327	- **Key behaviour.**
328	  - A hit is restamped with the serving commit (`restampCachedSearchSnapshotCommit`). Accepted caveat: after a rebase, co-change edges may reflect older history.
329	  - The cache envelope carries the internal metadata derivation needs (line counts, byte ranges, name lines, parameter names, signature types; `search_cache.go:44-96`), so a warm result equals a cold build.
330	- **The working tree is never cached.**
331	  - `worktreeSnapshotCacheable:100` returns `!options.Worktree`. The comment: *"A cleanliness comparison cannot pin Git's listing … A→B→A changes can therefore evade any pre/post recheck."*
332	  - ADR 0004 superseded ADR 0003 because `git status` can run filters chosen by the repository. It accepts that *"A working-tree query always reports a cache miss."*
333	  - Every inspection verb defaults to worktree mode (`cli/search.go:2809`, `impact.go:187`, `neighbors.go:202`, `def.go:260`, `explain.go:690`), so **by default the cache only helps `--head`**.
334	  - Worktree builds emit `W_WORKTREE_SNAPSHOT` (`provider.go:1874-1879`; wording fixed in `df38be28`).
335	- **Integrity.**
336	  - Keys must be 64 hex characters, reads go through `os.Root`, and writes require directories that do not redirect (`cache_entry.go`).
337	  - Ignore inputs are frozen once per transaction, capped at 128 inputs and 4 MiB; going over falls back to an uncached build (`cache_policy.go`; `search_cache.go:~270`).
338	  - `--force` publishes the new complete entry, then bumps the generation, then removes derived entries. An unreadable generation marker fails closed (`search_cache.go:~495-570`).
339	
340	### 3.5 Preindex vs worktree snapshot; the cold and warm paths
341	
342	- **Preindex** (`index`, `search_cache.go:PreindexProviderSnapshot:447`). It refuses worktree mode, requires a cache directory, and builds the complete full-profile snapshot of HEAD.
343	  - `persistVerifiedSearchSnapshot` (~579) writes the snapshot, then re-reads its SHA-256 through the same confined open and retries once.
344	  - This verify-by-digest step came in commit `d62dd2b4`, replacing a full decode that held about 1.2 GB of a 4.7 GB peak.
345	- **How search uses it** (`sem/search.go:SearchRepository:1109`).
346	  - The complete snapshot is loaded only when not in worktree mode and the cache is enabled (`search.go:1192-1202`). It is discarded if repository identity drifted (1214-1222).
347	  - A selective query derives an exact sub-view from it (1350-1363).
348	  - When every file is selected, the query uses the complete key, so `index` and all-files search share one artifact (1340-1345).
349	- **Default cold path** (worktree mode, which is what an agent following the normal guide gets):
350	  - Files are listed and scored cheaply. Only the selected files, 96 by default, are parsed with tree-sitter (§4.2).
351	  - Comment on the cap: *"Do NOT raise these bounds hoping for recall: MEASURED THE OPPOSITE"* (`search.go:defaultSearchIndexedFiles:2155-2179`).
352	- **Warm preindex path** (`search.go:2483-2575`). Conditions: an exactly matching preindex, `!Worktree`, `!Deep`, and grep-safe terms.
353	  - It runs one `GrepTreePathsIncludingBinary` over the commit, deliberately without `-I`, so the result is a superset of the files containing any term.
354	  - It keeps **every** matched or path-scoring file (`committedSearchFiles:3354`). The comment: *"MaxIndexedFiles is a cold selective-indexing guard, not a retrieval recall cap once the graph is preindexed."*
355	  - Corpus statistics are exact. The backend label is `git-tree-grep`.
356	  - **[correction]** This path is reachable only with `--head`. The search default is `Worktree:true`, so default users never take it.
357	
358	### 3.6 Ignore rules
359	
360	- **`.graphignore`** (`sem/ignore.go:733`). Uses gitignore syntax on top of `.gitignore`. This repository's own file skips vendored 30-54 MB `parser.c` blobs that had produced false "degraded" completeness.
361	- **Built-in credential deny-list.** Applied after the repository's excludes (`loadBuiltinSecretRules`, ~1063). Its digest is part of both cache keys.
362	- **Rule disclosure.** Rules from files inside the repository are disclosed to the reader; the user's own rules are not (`ignore.go:~44-60`).
363	- **Symlinks.** A symlinked `.graphignore` is refused via Lstat (~1328).

367	## 4. Stage 3 — the search pipeline, step by step
368	
369	The engine is `sem/search.go:searchRepository:1118`.
370	
371	**Defaults** (`search.go:31-58`):
372	
373	| Setting | Default |
374	|---|---|
375	| top-k | 10 |
376	| context lines | 8 |
377	| region lines | 80 |
378	| snippet lines | 6 |
379	| regions per file | 3 |
380	| indexed files | 96 (deep: 256) |
381	| query terms | 48 max |
382	| git-grep preselection threshold | 10,000 files |
383	| RRF k | 60 |
384	| diversity relevance ratio | 0.75 |
385	
386	The defaults carry a self-limiting comment: *"this output-budget choice is not evidence of end-to-end task savings."*
387	
388	### 4.1 Query parsing (`buildSearchQuery`, `search.go:6253-6421`)
389	
390	**Why it exists:** agents write prose ("where does the user log in"), but code spells it `login`, `userLogin` or `user_login`.
391	
392	- **Cleaning.** URL query strings and fragments are stripped (`stripSearchQueryURLState:1055`). Stop words (including "please" and "thanks"), terms shorter than 2 characters, and terms without letters or digits are dropped (`:1070-1085, 6258-6275`). A multi-word query written entirely in capitals is lowercased as emphasis (`searchQueryIsShouted:6459`).
393	- **Token variants** (`searchTokenVariants:6638`). Each token yields its whole lowercase form, its separator-split pieces and its camelCase pieces.
394	- **Weights:**
395	
396	  | Term kind | Weight | Source |
397	  |---|---|---|
398	  | Code-like token | 2.5 (1.4 if all caps and ≤4 letters) | `codeLikeSearchWeight:6579-6596` |
399	  | Fragment of a code-like token | 1.1 | — |
400	  | Plain prose word | 1.0 | — |
401	  | Morphological variant | 0.55 | — |
402	  | Inferred abbreviation | 0.55 | — |
403	
404	  "Code-like" means the token contains `_./:$+#`, starts with `--`, has an inner capital, or has 2+ capitals plus a lowercase letter (`codeLikeSearchToken:6598`).
405	- **Compound joins.**
406	  - A table maps prose pairs to identifiers, e.g. "log in"→login, "end point"→endpoint (`searchCompoundPhrases:5852-5890`).
407	  - A particle may sit up to 3 tokens away (`searchMaxCompoundGap=3`, `:5921`; `searchCompoundJoins:6102`).
408	  - Joined terms are *added* at weight 1.0, never substituted (`:6308-6324`). The motivating case was entireio/cli, where "logs a user in" returned the logging package.
409	- **Constraints** (`search_constraints.go:parseSearchConstraints:43`). Entities (identifier-shaped or capitalised words, at most 8) and phrases (quoted spans, plus 3- and 2-word windows, at most 16) become extra terms. They *"never decide admission"*; agreement only adds score after retrieval.
410	- **Stemming** (`morphologicalSearchTerms:6618`): -ization→-ize, -ification→-ify, -ing, -ed and plural -s, with length guards.
411	- **Abbreviations** (`searchTermAbbreviations:4294`). The map runs one way only, long form to short, e.g. address→addr.
412	  - Abbreviations enter as real terms, so they reach preselection and BM25 (`:6342-6373`).
413	  - The table is frequency-derived from 1.4M identifier tokens across 40 repositories. 23 of the original 74 entries failed the frequency filter; "delete→del" sank caddy-5870 (`:4278-4293`).
414	- **Finalisation.** Terms are sorted by weight, length, then alphabetically, and capped at 48 (`:6380-6398`). After corpus statistics, `withCorpusPresence:6514` removes words that no file contains, so *"inert evidence may not cost a document points."*
415	
416	### 4.2 Preselection (`preselectSearchFiles`, `search.go:2433-2966`)
417	
418	**Why it exists:** parsing an entire large repository per query is too slow. Grep-like signals pick a small, high-recall set of files to parse.
419	
420	One of four routes runs:
421	
422	1. **Warm preindex** (`--head` with a matching `index`). One git tree grep. **Every** match is kept (§3.5), with alias queries using bounded regex scans (`search_alias_grep.go:12-16`: at most 4 alias scans and a 128 KiB pattern). Files are sorted by `2*pathScore + pathPrior`.
423	2. **Small repository.** If every file fits under the cap, or `--index-all-files` is set, every file is selected and corpus counts are exact (`:2575-2579`).
424	3. **Large worktree** (10,000 or more files, `shouldUseGitGrepPreselection:3451`).
425	   - A git *index* grep samples with up to 6 direct patterns plus 1 derived (`:3504-3531`).
426	   - Each file gets a provisional score of `2*pathScore + matchedWeight + pathPrior`, plus a coverage bonus.
427	   - It content-scans a shortlist of 4× the cap. These posting lists are partial and are discarded for idf (`:2958-2963`).
428	4. **Default cold content pass** (`scoreFile:2812-2887`).
429	   - Workers: 1 on the committed tree, up to 8 for a worktree.
430	   - Each file scores `2*pathSearchScore + matchedWeight + searchPathPrior`, using an ASCII Aho-Corasick matcher (`search_matcher.go:28`).
431	   - Constraint evidence adds +1 per entity and +2 per ordered phrase (`search_preselection.go:searchFileConstraintEvidence:223`).
432	   - Coverage adds `4*matched/queryWeight` (`applySearchFileCoverage:2351`).
433	
434	**Progressive selection** (`search_preselection.go`) applies only when the default cap of 96 is in force and more files qualify.
435	
436	- Path, content and constraint rankings are fused with reciprocal-rank fusion, k=60 (`fuseSearchPreselectionEvidence:44`).
437	- `selectProgressiveSearchFiles:93` starts at 96 and doubles up to 4× (384). It stops once all three hold:
438	  - confidence `1 - rrf[next]/rrf[last] ≥ 0.15`;
439	  - weighted term coverage of 1;
440	  - top-level-directory diversity of 1 (target 3 directories).
441	
442	**The cap** (`defaultSearchIndexedFiles:2155-2179`) is `min(256, max(96, min(topK,256)×3))`. The comment records measured gold-file recall of 76.9% at 96 files, 73.1% at 256 and 69.2% at 1024: *"Preselection is a useful FILTER, not the recall limit."*
443	
444	**Registration bridge** (`:2968-3010`). It adds the files that define handlers named in `commands/*.json`: at most 8 handlers and 64 parses.
445	
446	After preselection, the selected files are parsed into a selective graph snapshot (or derived from the preindex). Repository identity and HEAD are re-checked for drift (`:1371-1424`).
447	
448	### 4.3 Corpus statistics and idf (the #291 fix)
449	
450	**Why it exists:** BM25's idf says how rare a word is. Computed over the *preselected* files, which were chosen *because* they contain the query words, idf collapses toward zero and ranking degrades to noise.
451	
452	- **Two passes.** Pass 1 over the selected files counts per-term file DF, content DF, files inspected and read failures (`search.go:1471-1514`). Its comment: *"An unread selected file is UNKNOWN, not zero."* Pass 2 builds candidates (`:1517-1528`).
453	- **Choice** (`searchChooseIDFStatistics:4012-4022`, called at `:1554`; `searchCorpusIDFStatistics:4037-4050`).
454	  - If an exact repository-wide corpus is known, idf uses repository-wide document frequency over every text file's content. Exact corpora come from the warm git-tree-grep, a small repository, or a complete cold content pass with no read failures.
455	  - Otherwise it falls back to the sample.
456	  - Any read failure revokes exactness (`:4016-4018`).
457	- **Rationale** (`:4024-4036`): *"The selected files are the ones preselection kept BECAUSE they contain the most query words, so within them nearly every query word is common and its idf collapses toward zero… A Git-narrowed or bounded pass cannot know it, and keeps the sample statistics."*
458	- **Commits:** `7a372859` ("BM25 idf from repository-wide document frequencies") and `4a5f46b4` ("an unread file revokes exact corpus statistics"). That these are PR #291 is **[unverified]**.
459	
460	### 4.4 Candidates (`candidatesForFile`, `search.go:3534-3593`)
461	
462	**Why it exists:** results should be meaningful units — a whole function, or the part of a giant class that matched — not arbitrary line windows.
463	
464	- **Cutting.**
465	  - A symbol whose span, including leading documentation, fits in 80 lines becomes one candidate.
466	  - Larger symbols are split into regions around hits (`regionsAroundHits:5819`, 8 lines of context). Each region is credited to the smallest containing callable (`attributeSearchRegion:3610`). Otherwise *"a 3,000-line class scores its name bonus at every matching line."*
467	  - Lines outside any symbol form symbol-free regions.
468	  - A file that matches only by path gets a candidate for its first lines.
469	- **Focus line.** The line with the most weighted term matches (`:6797`); the snippet is centred on it (`:6816`). The symbol's NameLine is carried through (`:3985`).
470	- **Base score** (`makeSearchCandidate:3932-3994`) is path score + symbol score + path prior.
471	  - **`pathSearchScore`** (`:6829-6845`): +2.5×w for a basename hit, else +1.25×w for a full-path hit.
472	  - **`symbolSearchScore`** (`:7040-7090`):
473	    - kind base: function/method +2, type-like +0.75, block/document −1.5, section −0.5;
474	    - exact-symbol bonus (`exactSymbolBonus:7109`): 14 for callables, 6 for containers and constants in multi-word queries, 0 for a constructor named after its own type (`GsonBuilder.GsonBuilder` had taken ranks 1–2 in 43 Java instances);
475	    - per term: name equals term +6×w, name-token match +3×w, signature match +1.5×w;
476	    - an exact registration alias +6×w.
477	  - **`searchPathPrior`** (`:6847-6901`):
478	    - `/src/`, `/include/`, `/lib/`, `/packages/`: +0.5;
479	    - `.github/workflows/`: −6, unless the query is about CI;
480	    - other `.github/`: −12 (an issue template had ranked first);
481	    - third-party code: −5;
482	    - **test paths: −12**, unless the query asks for tests (*"was -1.5 — far too weak… -12 reliably sinks the test… Not excluded outright"*);
483	    - docs: −6;
484	    - generated code: −6.
485	
486	    Test intent is read only from words the caller actually wrote (`searchQuerySupplied:6993`).
487	
488	### 4.5 Scoring (`scoreSearchCandidates`, `search.go:4052-4134`)
489	
490	**Why it exists:** combine "the body talks about this", "the name *is* this" and "the structure says this is the edit site" into one comparable number.
491	
492	- **idf** = `ln(1 + (N−df+0.5)/(df+0.5)) × weight` (`:4065`). A term no file contains is left out entirely, *"never a penalty"* (`:4067-4075`).
493	- **BM25** with k1=1.2 and b=0.75: `idf·tf·2.2 / (tf + 1.2·(0.25 + 0.75·dl/avgdl))` (`:4093-4094`). `avgdl` is computed over candidates.
494	- **Main formula** (`:4116-4117`, verified):
495	
496	  ```go
497	  candidate.score = candidate.baseScore + bm25 + 7*coverage + minFloat64(24, codeTokenBonus)
498	  candidate.score += searchNameCoverageWeight * searchNameTermCoverage(candidate.result, q, idf)
499	  ```
500	
501	  - `coverage` is the idf-weighted share of query terms matched.
502	  - `codeTokenBonus` adds 6×w per matched term whose weight is at least 2.
503	  - One-line data declarations (3 lines or fewer, no exact-symbol match, name not covering the query) get BM25 ×0.4 and bonus ×0.5 (`:4096-4111`).
504	- **Name coverage, weight 10** (`searchNameCoverageWeight = 10.0`, `:4531`). The comment: *"Sized against the existing document-coverage weight of 7: the identifier is the stronger evidence."*
505	  - `searchNameTermCoverage:4157-4191` counts distinct non-alias query terms in the symbol name's tokens, tolerating plurals, and saturates at 3: `min(matched,3)/3`. One, two and three matched terms add +3.33, +6.67 and +10.
506	  - It is deliberately **not** idf-weighted (`:4166-4173`, citing hugo#12171, where `getPagesInSection` was absent from the top 20).
507	- **Structural adjustment** (`searchStructuralAdjustment:4598-4639`):
508	  - executable kinds +3, containers −3;
509	  - name covers at least half the query +4;
510	  - qualified name contains 2+ code-like terms +8, one +2;
511	  - query names the symbol as a dotted call +15.
512	- **Constraint agreement** (`search_constraints.go:294-339`): entity share ×1.5 plus phrase share ×1.5, plus 1.0 if both match, capped at 4.
513	- **All terms matched:** +2 and the signal `all-query-terms` (`:4129-4132`).
514	- **Caller boost** (`searchGraphCallerBoosts:4676`, applied at `:1567`). `min(8, 2.6·log2(1 + distinct non-test callers))` over CALLS, ASYNC_CALLS and CONSTRUCTS edges with confidence ≥0.7. It is halved when the only evidence is body text (`:4731-4750`).
515	
516	### 4.6 Expansions
517	
518	**Why they exist:** the edit site often does not contain the query's words. Its caller, callee or neighbour does.
519	
520	Every expanded row is capped just below the row that produced it (`search.go:4655`, verified):
521	
522	```go
523	func derivedSearchScore(parent, proposed float64) float64 { return minFloat64(parent-0.01, proposed) }
524	```
525	
526	The four expansions:
527	
528	1. **Graph neighbours** (`expandGraphCandidates:4778-4913`).
529	   - Seeds: the top 10 distinct symbols.
530	   - Edges: confidence ≥0.7, followed in both directions, across CALLS, CONSTRUCTS, ASYNC_CALLS, IMPORTS, EXTENDS, INHERITS, IMPLEMENTS, OVERRIDES, USES_TYPE, TESTS, CONFIGURES and SIMILAR_TO.
531	   - Proposed score: `inherit + 2.2·confidence + pathPrior + callerBoost`, where inherit is:
532	     - 0.28×seed by default;
533	     - 0.55×seed if the neighbour carries query terms;
534	     - 0.85×seed for a call edge of confidence ≥0.8 whose name matches a term (the "vocabulary-gap bridge").
535	   - At most 20 rows.
536	2. **Identifier usages** (`expandIdentifierUsageCandidates:4991-5146`).
537	   - Seeds: hits scoring at least 0.35× the best whose names are compound identifiers of 6+ characters.
538	   - Whole-word uses are found by git tree grep, skipping imports and the definition. At most 3 are kept per seed and 32 overall.
539	   - Score: `derived(seed, 0.9·seed + pathPrior)`.
540	3. **Same-container neighbours** (`expandSameContainerNeighborCandidates:5221-5328`).
541	   - Takes the previous and next callable in the same container around strong callable hits.
542	   - The comment: lifecycle code splits into *"tick -> dispatch -> run"* without explicit call edges.
543	   - Score: `derived(seed, 0.85·seed)`. At most 24 rows.
544	4. **Same-file bridges** (`expandSameFileBridgeCandidates:5350-5444`).
545	   - Fills a short gap between two strong regions in the same container.
546	   - A bridge justified only by an inferred alias in the path is rejected.
547	   - Score: `derived(max(L,R), 0.45·(L+R))`. At most 20 rows.
548	
549	Graph neighbours are merged and sorted first. The other three seed from that sorted set (`:1571-1607`), so a derived row can seed further derived rows.
550	
551	### 4.7 Priors, dedup and diverse selection (`search.go:1608-1684`)
552	
553	**Why it exists:** avoid ten hits that are the same function in `src/` and `dist/`, or ten regions from one file.
554	
555	- **Mirror dedup** (`search_mirror_dedup.go:14`). Drops exact copies (same kind, qualified name and body hash) on related paths such as src vs dist. Sibling monorepo packages are kept.
556	- **File-class prior** (`search_file_class.go:485-539, 788-810`). Multiplies positive scores only:
557	  - docs, vendored, generated and data/config: ×0.5, so such a file *"must be twice as relevant as the best source hit to win"*;
558	  - examples, `.d.ts`/`.pyi` mirrors and fixtures: ×0.75;
559	  - one-line uninitialised declarations: ×0.6.
560	
561	  Each prior is waived when the query asks for that class.
562	- **Boilerplate prior ×0.6** (`search_boilerplate.go:44, 111`). Applies to `toString`/`__repr__`/`String`, trivial accessors, and literal tables.
563	  - Order matters (`:1630-1638`): the additive caller boost runs *before* the multiplicative priors, so a demoted file loses its graph boost too.
564	- **Near-duplicate collapse** (`search_near_dupe.go:46`). Same basename with identical normalised text, or version-segment paths with Jaccard ≥0.9. The survivor shows "+N similar".
565	- **Diverse selection** (`selectDiverseCandidates`, `search.go:5617-5669`, called via `search_prose_parent.go:selectSearchCandidates:181`).
566	  - Greedy pick on `score − 0.8·(regions already taken from this file) − 4·(same qualified name taken) − 2·(same basename taken)` (`:5716-5733`).
567	  - At most 3 per file. A region overlapping a chosen one by 60% or more is skipped.
568	  - **Unseen-file reserve:** until ceil(topK/2) distinct files are chosen, only one region per file is allowed while a strong new-file hit exists. The comment: *"Give the agent one strong location from each candidate file before spending the remaining result budget on additional regions in files it has already seen."*
569	  - Ties break deterministically (`searchCandidateLess:5761`).
570	- **`--deep` hybrid fusion** (`selectHybridCandidates:5469-5550`). RRF of the sparse window list with the semantic list. Reported scores are restored to the semantic scale, because overwriting them with 1/rank had *"destroyed exactly that signal."*
571	- **Fix site over leading test** (`search_testrank.go:promoteFixSiteOverLeadingTest:81`). Moves the best editable hit above a test file at rank 1 without changing any score. Even with −12, a test led on 3 of 30 rep30 instances.
572	- **Ranking finalised.** Ranks are assigned and scores rounded to 4 decimals (`:1674-1684`). **Multi-resolution** (`search_multi_resolution.go:5-28`) is strictly additive: prose passages fill only empty slots, and code results are never touched.
573	
574	### 4.8 The post-ranking passes, in order (`search.go:1689-2060`)
575	
576	**Why they exist:** a ranked list is not yet an answer. The agent needs the right amount of source per row, inside a byte budget, plus enough context to avoid a follow-up Read.
577	
578	The sequence is fixed:
579	
580	1. **Doc-comment re-anchor** (`search_reanchor.go:129`). Moves the focus line from the doc comment to the code, for example `focus=19->26`. *"move the ANCHOR, not the score… Ranking is deliberately untouched."*
581	2. **Section labels** priced early (`search_section.go:205`). They had once landed outside the budget (6170 > 6000 bytes).
582	3. **Byte fit** (`fitSearchResultsToBudget:2182`). Decides *how many* rows fit.
583	4. **Enclosure planning** (`search_enclosure.go:planSearchEnclosures:544`) and **snippet allocation** (`allocateSearchSnippets:1001`). Decide how the bytes are spent (§4.9).
584	5. **Re-anchor funding gate** (`search.go:1767-1789`). A body gained only by re-anchoring is kept only if it preserves source (vuejs__core-11870).
585	6. **Budget spend** (`spendRemainingSearchBudget:1276`). Only with `--full-unit-top` or `--callee-hop`.
586	7. **Prose passages**, then a **truncation counter** that runs before ranks are renumbered.
587	8. **Callee hop** (`:1809-1836`). Placed before span merge so a same-file callee can fold into its caller.

588	9. **Span merge** (§4.10), **related sites** (§4.11), **covering test and type card** (`search_contract.go`), **signature types**, **closed set**, **literal cluster**, **file outline**, **VERIFY** (§4.15) and **container map**.
589	10. **Prose cleanup.**
590	11. **Complete certification, last** (`certifyAlreadyCompleteSearchResults`, `search_enclosure.go:365-460`). It runs after every merge *"so assigning it earlier can't spend a sibling's source."*
591	
592	### 4.9 Enclosure, full units and complete bodies (`search_enclosure.go`)
593	
594	**Why it exists** (`:8-27`): *"95.9% of billed tokens are context re-read… a mean turn re-reads ~47.5k tokens."* One avoided follow-up read is worth far more than the bytes of a body.
595	
596	- **Constants:**
597	  - `defaultSearchEnclosureMaxLines=160` (`:35`).
598	  - `searchEnclosureHeadRanks=5` (`:41`): the only ranks eligible for bodies, and never demoted.
599	  - `searchHeadWindowLines=60` (`:71`): measured median read window 50 lines, median gap 42.
600	  - `searchRenderedSnippetHeadRanks=2` (`:194`).
601	- **Picking a plan.** The allocator scores every demotion cut on rank-discounted value, because a greedy fill is *"not monotone in the cut"* (`:1048-1070`). Demoted rows keep their declaration line where it fits: `tersifySearchResultKeepingDeclaration` (`search_decl_line.go:141-170`), called from `planWithDemotionFrom` (`:1417-1427`).
602	- **Signals:**
603	  - `complete-symbol` promises "you need no follow-up read".
604	  - `head-window` marks a 60-line window and never carries complete.
605	  - `full-unit` and `unit-elided` are the forced-unit signals.
606	
607	  If the focus line lies outside the enclosure, the row gets head-window, never completeness (the carbon-2752 bug, `:868-880`).
608	- **`--full-unit-top`** (design note `:73-99`).
609	  - Caps: `searchFullUnitMaxLines=400` (`:105`). Rank 2 and below are admitted only within 15% of rank 1's score (`searchFullUnitGapRatio`, `:200`).
610	  - `seatForcedSearchUnits` (`:1199-1270`) guarantees *"a forced unit may never reduce any other rank's rendered source"* (redis-11734 had lost `bitposCommand`).
611	  - Elision is printed as a separate note line, never inline, because agents copy bodies verbatim as `old_string` (`:225-231`).
612	- **Certification rules** (`:365-460`). `complete-symbol` is granted only when all of these hold:
613	  - the row is in the original body head;
614	  - the snippet is exactly the symbol's span, byte for byte;
615	  - the kind is enclosable and the row is not elided;
616	  - the signal's bytes fit in spare budget.
617	- **Nameless locator** (`search_locator_window.go:SearchLocatorWindow:50`). A demoted hit with no enclosing symbol keeps up to 6 lines of source instead of a bare `N. path:line`; 21 of 238 rows (8.8%) had been printing bare.

619	### 4.10 Span merge (`search_span_merge.go`)
620	
621	**Why it exists** (`:8-35`): in 40% of 113 Opus payloads, two hits in the same file were less than 40 lines apart. The tool arm made 19.6% more Read calls even though total calls fell 14.5%.
622	
623	- **Limits.** `searchSpanMergeMaxGapLines = 40` (`:59`, verified), `searchSpanMergeMaxSpanLines = 80` (`:64`). The merged row gets the signal `contiguous-span`.
624	- **Rules.**
625	  - Each merge is costed against the ceiling before it is committed.
626	  - *"Merging never REORDERS"* (`:50-53`).
627	  - Only rows that are complete-symbol and have no section are eligible.
628	- **Survivor.** The best-ranked member survives and records `MergedRanks`, `MergedDeclLines` and `MergedDeclStarts` (`search_decl_line.go:searchMergedDeclarations:187`). This is how absorbed declarations are tracked.

630	### 4.11 Related sites and displacement (`search_related.go`)
631	
632	**Why it exists** (`:9-23`): in 31 lost instances, the missing site was always one graph hop from a surfaced hit.
633	
634	- **Kinds:**
635	  - caller, shown at the call-site line (`:435`);
636	  - sibling: overrides, same-name members, or co-members of a unit with at most 12 members (`:474`);
637	  - near-dupe: SIMILAR_TO matches plus same-file clones (`:588`).
638	
639	  Outgoing calls are excluded (`:39-41`). Limits are 4 sites and 12 candidates (`:48, 54`).
640	- **This commit (`0d92152d`).** Adds `searchRelatedDeclarationLine` (`:454-460`). It uses `NameLine()` when that line falls inside the symbol span, else StartLine. Sibling and near-dupe locators now point at the declaration name instead of a decorator line.
641	- **Entries.** One-line locators with signal `related:<kind>`, skipped when the site is already shown (`searchRelatedResult:783, 815`).
642	- **Funding** (`mergeSearchRelatedSites:849-899`). The payload never grows: each site displaces at most one ranked hit, and ranks 1-5 are never displaced.

645	### 4.12 Context blocks (`search_blocks.go`)
646	
647	- **One ceiling** (`:15-23`). `--max-context-bytes` funds ranking, the covering test, the type card and signature types. The container map, literal cluster, VERIFY and closed set have their own caps:
648	
649	  | Block | Cap | Source |
650	  |---|---|---|
651	  | closed set | 420 B | `search_closedset.go:54` |
652	  | literal cluster | 560 B | `search_literals.go:43` |

658	  - Off: container map, signature types and type card. Turning them on measured 23.1 turns vs 21.0 and +14-19% cost.
659	  - On: literal cluster, VERIFY, closed set and covering test, because each replaces a tool call the agent would otherwise make.
660	- **Ordering.** The reading order (`:46-71`) and the yield order under pressure (`:76-108`: type card → map → signature types → covering test) are fixed. The head and every file's last mention never yield.
